You need context awareness, consistency across sections, and proof that your responses meet compliance and AI governance expectations. That is where Inventive AI supports proposal, sales, and security teams working under tight deadlines. Here is how Inventive AI helps you submit stronger, more defensible responses: Context Engine: Unlike basic chat-based tools that generate generic answers, Inventive AI's multi-layer reasoning engine reads the entire RFP before drafting responses. It understands dependencies between sections, so your AI governance answer aligns with your deletion workflow, consent model, and security posture. Conflict Detection: Inventive AI automatically flags inconsistent claims across your response. If one section states fully automated deletion and another implies manual approval, the system highlights the mismatch before submission, reducing compliance and credibility risks. Outdated Content Detection: Large answer libraries often contain expired certifications or legacy regulatory references. Inventive AI scans your knowledge sources and surfaces outdated or non-compliant content, helping teams avoid sending incorrect information. 2X Higher-Quality Responses : Inventive AI uses specialized AI agents to interpret intent, structure strategic answers, and improve clarity and completeness. The result is responses that read like they were written by a subject matter expert, not assembled from disconnected fragments. Simple and Easy-to-Use Interface: With a 100 percent adoption rate among its existing customers and a ranking as the number one easiest-to-use RFP software on G2, Inventive AI helps proposal, sales, and security teams get started quickly, even without previous experience with AI tools. When privacy RFPs demand accuracy, consistency, and proof rather than promises, Inventive AI helps your team respond with confidence. Still coordinating inputs from legal, security, and engineering teams manually? See how Inventive AI delivers 2× more accurate, consistent responses with less back-and-forth. Book a Demo FAQs 1. How long should a data privacy software RFP response be? Length should reflect the complexity of the buyer's requirements rather than a fixed page count. Enterprise privacy RFP responses often range from 25 to 80 pages, depending on regulatory scope and technical depth. Focus on completeness and clarity instead of adding unnecessary narrative. 2. Who should be involved in preparing a privacy RFP response? A strong response typically requires input from security, legal, engineering, and product teams. Proposal managers coordinate timelines and messaging, while subject matter experts validate technical and compliance details before submission. 3. How can you reduce back-and-forth questions after submission? Anticipate clarification requests by addressing assumptions directly in your response. Define technical terms, explain architectural limitations, and provide supporting metrics so evaluators do not need to request additional detail. 4. What documents should you attach to a privacy RFP response? Common attachments include security certifications, penetration test summaries, data processing agreements, sub-processor lists, and architectural diagrams. Including these proactively signals preparedness and reduces procurement delays. 5. How do you prepare for a privacy-focused vendor demo after submitting your response? Align your demo agenda with the highest-weighted evaluation criteria in the RFP. Be ready to walk through deletion workflows, reporting dashboards, and governance controls in a structured, time-bound format that matches your written claims.

body_text: View All News Aptiv Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results August 4, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Strong Operating Performance and Significant Progress Diversifying Towards Non-Auto Markets SCHAFFHAUSEN, Switzerland--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Aptiv PLC (NYSE: APTV), a global industrial technology company, today reported financial results for the second quarter of 2026. Second Quarter Financial Highlights Include : U.S. GAAP revenue of $3.3 billion, an increase of 2% Adjusted revenue growth of 2% U.S. GAAP net income from continuing operations of $298 million Adjusted EBITDA of $613 million U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.40 Adjusted net income per share of $1.63 Completed the spin-off of Electrical Distribution Systems segment Electrical Distribution Systems segment classified as discontinued operations for all periods presented Received cash dividend of $1.9 billion in connection with the spin-off Year-to-Date Financial Highlights Include : U.S. GAAP revenue of $6.3 billion, an increase of 2% Adjusted revenue growth of 1% U.S. GAAP net income from continuing operations of $427 million Adjusted EBITDA of $1,106 million U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $2.01 Adjusted net income per share of $2.56 "We delivered solid results in the second quarter, our first as New Aptiv, with a reacceleration in revenue growth and margin expansion year-over-year,” said Kevin Clark, chair and chief executive officer. “In addition, we continued to demonstrate progress on many of our strategic initiatives, including double digit revenue growth in Non-Automotive revenues, advancing our presence in the Robotics market from partnerships to commercial stage, and securing a major Drone market commercial win in early July. While the macroeconomic landscape for Automotive remains dynamic and customer mix has presented as an incremental headwind, we remain committed to delivering continued revenue growth and strong operating performance this year. Moreover, our strong belief in the long-term value of our business and opportunity for growth across markets has reinforced our commitment in returning capital to shareholders, with half of our expected cash flow for the year already having been allocated towards share repurchases, a level we see continuing for the next few years." Second Quarter 2026 Results For the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company reported U.S. GAAP revenue of $3.3 billion, an increase of 2% from the prior year period. Adjusted for currency exchange and commodity movements, revenue increased by 2% in the second quarter. This reflects growth of 10% in North America, 6% in Asia Pacific, which includes growth of 5% in China, partially offset by declines of 8% in EMEA and 4% in South America, our smallest region. The Company reported second quarter 2026 U.S. GAAP net income from continuing operations of $298 million, net income margin from continuing operations of 9.1% and earnings from continuing operations of $1.40 per diluted share, compared to U.S. GAAP net income from continuing operations of $265 million, net income margin from continuing operations of 8.3% and earnings from continuing operations of $1.21 per diluted share in the prior year period. Second quarter Adjusted Net Income totaled $345 million, or earnings of $1.63 per diluted share, compared to $285 million, or $1.31 per diluted share, in the prior year period. The Company reported second quarter Adjusted EBITDA of $613 million, compared to $547 million in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 18.7%, compared to 17.1% in the prior year period, primarily reflecting increased volumes and favorable impacts of foreign currency exchange, partially offset by increased commodity costs. The Company reported second quarter Adjusted Operating Income of $473 million, compared to $410 million in the prior year period. Adjusted Operating Income margin was 14.4%, compared to 12.8% in the prior year period. Depreciation and amortization expense totaled $195 million, compared to $190 million in the prior year period. Interest expense for the second quarter totaled $62 million, compared to $92 million in the prior year period. Tax expense in the second quarter of 2026 was $52 million, compared to $16 million in the prior year period. Net cash flow provided by operating activities from continuing operations totaled $137 million in the second quarter, compared to $326 million in the prior year period. The Company generated Free Cash Flow of $12 million in the second quarter, compared to $219 million generated in the prior year period. Year-to-Date 2026 Results For the six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company reported U.S. GAAP revenue of $6.3 billion, an increase of 2% from the prior year period. Adjusted for currency exchange and commodity movements, revenue increased by 1% during the period. This reflects growth of 9% in North America and 1% in Asia Pacific, which includes a decline of 4% in China, partially offset by declines of 7% in EMEA and 3% in South America, our smallest region. The Company reported 2026 year-to-date U.S. GAAP net income from continuing operations of $427 million, net income margin from continuing operation of 6.8% and earnings from continuing operations of $2.01 per diluted share, compared to U.S. GAAP net income from continuing operations of $125 million, net income margin from continuing operation of 2.0% and earnings from continuing operations of $0.55 per diluted share in the prior year period. Year-to-date Adjusted Net Income totaled $545 million, or earnings of $2.56 per diluted share, compared to $517 million, or $2.30 per diluted share, in the prior year period. For the 2026 year-to-date period, The Company reported Adjusted EBITDA of $1,106 million, compared to $1,059 million in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.5%, compared to 17.1% in the prior year period, primarily reflecting increased volumes and favorable impacts of foreign currency exchange, partially offset by increased commodity costs. The Company reported Adjusted Operating Income of $829 million for the year-to-date 2026 period, compared to $789 million in the prior year period. Adjusted Operating Income margin was 13.1%, compared to 12.8% in the prior year period. Depreciation and amortization expense totaled $384 million, compared to $379 million in the prior year period. Interest expense for the year-to-date period totaled $146 million, compared to $185 million in the prior year period. Tax expense in the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $94 million. Tax expense in the six months ended June 30, 2025 was $342 million, which primarily reflects an increase to valuation allowances of approximately $300 million on deferred tax assets impacted by the OECD Administrative Guidance issued in the first quarter of 2025. Net cash flow provided by operating activities from continuing operations totaled $82 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $531 million in the prior year period. The Company reported negative Free Cash Flow of $196 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $264 million generated in the prior year period. Reconciliations of Adjusted Revenue Growth, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Operating Income, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Net Income Per Share and Free Cash Flow, which are non-GAAP measures, to the most directly comparable financial measures, respectively, calculated and presented in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (“GAAP”) are provided in the attached supplemental schedules. Debt Redemptions and Share Repurchases In April 2026, the Company redeemed $1,847 million of aggregate principal amount of certain senior notes principally utilizing proceeds from the cash distribution received from Versigent in connection with the spin-off. The Company repurchased and retired 4.1 million shares for $250 million in the second quarter of 2026, bringing the year-to-date total to $325 million. As of June 30, 2026, $1.8 billion remained available for future share repurchases under the Company’s existing authorization. EDS Spin-Off As previously disclosed, the spin-off of the Company’s former Electrical Distribution Systems segment into a new independent publicly traded company, Versigent PLC, was completed on April 1, 2026. The results of the Electrical Distribution Systems business through April 1, 2026 are presented as discontinued operations separate from the Company’s continuing operations for all periods presented. In connection with the spin-off, Aptiv received a dividend of approximately $1.9 billion from Versigent, which the Company used to opportunistically redeem outstanding debt prior to maturity. Q3 and Full Year 2026 Outlook The Company’s third quarter and full year 2026 financial guidance is as follows. This reflects Aptiv without the EDS business, which is presented as discontinued operations. A replay will be available two hours following the conference call. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Information This press release contains information about Aptiv’s financial results which are not presented in accordance with GAAP. Specifically, Adjusted Revenue Growth, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Operating Income, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Net Income Per Share and Free Cash Flow are non-GAAP financial measures. Adjusted Revenue Growth represents the year-over-year change in reported net sales relative to the comparable period, excluding the impact on net sales from currency exchange, commodity movements, acquisitions, divestitures and other transactions. Adjusted EBITDA represents net income (loss) before depreciation and amortization (including asset impairments), interest expense, income tax (expense) benefit, other income (expense), net, equity income (loss), net of tax, income (loss) from discontinued operations, restructuring and other special items. Adjusted EBITDA margin is defined as Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of net sales. Adjusted Operating Income represents net income (loss) before interest expense, other income (expense), net, income tax (expense) benefit, equity income (loss), net of tax, income (loss) from discontinued operations, amortization, restructuring, separation costs related to the spin-off of the Electrical Distribution Systems business, other acquisition and portfolio project costs (which includes costs incurred to integrate acquired businesses and to plan and execute product portfolio transformation actions, including business and product acquisitions and divestitures), goodwill and other asset impairments, compensation expense related to acquisitions and gains (losses) on business divestitures and other transactions. Adjusted Operating Income margin is defined as Adjusted Operating Income as a percentage of net sales. Adjusted Net Income represents net income (loss) attributable to Aptiv before income (loss) from discontinued operations, amortization, restructuring and other special items, including the tax impact thereon. Adjusted Net Income Per Share represents Adjusted Net Income divided by the Weighted Average Number of Diluted Shares Outstanding for the period. Free cash flow represents cash provided by (used in) operating activities from continuing operations less capital expenditures. Management believes the non-GAAP financial measures used in this press release are useful to both management and investors in their analysis of the Company’s financial position, results of operations and liquidity. In particular, management believes Adjusted Revenue Growth, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Operating Income, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Net Income Per Share and Free Cash Flow are useful measures in assessing the Company’s ongoing financial performance that, when reconciled to the corresponding GAAP measure, provide improved comparability between periods through the exclusion of certain items that management believes are not indicative of the Company’s core operating performance and that may obscure underlying business results and trends. Management also uses these non-GAAP financial measures for internal planning and forecasting purposes. Such non-GAAP financial measures are reconciled to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures in the attached supplemental schedules at the end of this press release. Non-GAAP measures should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for our reported results prepared in accordance with GAAP and, as calculated, may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. title: Globe Life Announces New Share Repurchase Authorization
summary: Globe Life Inc. (NYSE:GL) announced a new authorization, effective August 15, 2026, to repurchase up to $2.5 billion of common stock in the future under the Company's existing share repurchase prog...
body_text: Globe Life Announces New Share Repurchase Authorization August 10, 2026 McKinney, Texas Globe Life Inc. (NYSE:GL) announced a new authorization, effective August 15, 2026, to repurchase up to $2.5 billion of common stock in the future under the Company's existing share repurchase program. This authorization was approved by Globe Life's Board of Directors during its regular quarterly board meeting on August 5, 2026, and replaces any previous authorizations. "This authorization reflects the Board's enduring confidence in Globe Life's ability to create long-term value. Our insurance operations have consistently generated reliable free cash flow for the parent company across varying economic environments. Since launching our repurchase program in 1986, we have returned nearly $11.5 billion to shareholders through buybacks," said Matt Darden, Co-Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. Frank Svoboda, Co-Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, noted, "Our capital allocation strategy remains disciplined and consistent. We prioritize the full funding of our insurance operations' growth before deploying excess capital. In the absence of more accretive investment opportunities, and subject to prevailing market conditions, we expect to continue returning capital to shareholders through share repurchases, in keeping with our commitment to maximizing long-term shareholder value." Globe Life Inc. is a holding company specializing in life and supplemental health insurance for the middle-income market distributed through multiple channels, including direct to consumer and exclusive and independent agencies. For additional information contact: Stephen Mota Vice President, Investor Relations Phone: 972-569-3627 FAX: 972-569-3680 Investors@globe.life Website: https://investors.globelifeinsurance.com

title: Intapp announces re-architected Compliance and Time solutions, with Intapp Celeste at the core
summary: Intapp announces governed agentic AI capabilities powered by Intapp Celeste in Intake, Conflicts, Terms, and Time.
body_text: New, agent-first solutions – Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste – bring agentic AI that knows how the firm works to the workflows behind profitable, compliant growth, from business acceptance and client risk management to timekeeping and revenue governance PALO ALTO, Calif. — August 19, 2026 — Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA), the governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries, today announced the availability of Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste – its Compliance and Time solutions re-architected with Intapp Celeste and agentic workflows at their core. Available to firms through a new entitlement, these solutions bring the agentic capabilities of Celeste into the client acceptance, risk, and revenue processes law firms and other professional firms run in Intapp Intake, Conflicts, Terms, and Time. They handle the repetitive parts of that work so people can focus their time on work that requires human judgment. AI is changing the economics of law firms and other professional firms by squeezing them in two directions at once. On the risk side, growth through M&A, consolidation, and lateral moves makes onboarding new business and managing risk increasingly complex. The volume of forms, searches, and obligation checks required to support that growth can quickly outpace the capacity of expert teams, whose expertise is scarce and takes years to develop. When highly skilled professionals spend too much time on repetitive tasks instead of judgment, firms face a difficult trade-off between moving intake forward quickly and maintaining rigorous risk management. Revenue is the other side of the equation. As AI helps people work faster, the billable hour — the backbone of most firm revenue — comes under pressure. Clients increasingly expect pricing that reflects those efficiencies, and firms will need room to experiment with new fee structures to deliver it. This experimentation will only work with the right data and insights behind it. Without visibility into how AI-assisted work and other hours add up at the matter level, firms lack the insight needed to make critical decisions about what to scope, what to charge, who to staff, and where to invest in AI. Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste meet both pressures head-on, bringing agentic AI directly into these workflows using each firm’s own data and rules. How Celeste helps Compliance Inside Intake, Conflicts, and Terms, Celeste takes on the repetitive parts of intake and risk work so experts can get to the analysis and judgment. Faster, cleaner intake. Celeste fills in request forms using information from the emails people already share, then flags missing or incomplete data before anything gets submitted. The busywork behind each decision, handled. Celeste builds the search strategy, maps corporate trees, runs the searches, and triages what comes back for expert review. Client obligations that don’t slip. Celeste reads outside counsel guidelines, matches them to the right client, pulls out key terms, and files the attributes that matter. Answers right where you work. Ask Celeste a question or kick off a playbook from a prompt inside Intake, Conflicts, Terms, or directly in Outlook. How Celeste helps Time Inside Time, Celeste captures hours that would otherwise be lost, helps prevent revenue leakage, and gives firms a clearer view of what each matter is actually worth. Time entries ready to bill. Celeste drafts complete entries from the work it already sees and fills in the gaps. Revenue governance without the manual work. With agentic time entry, Celeste writes each narrative for you and can rewrite the ones you enter yourself. Both stay compliant with outside counsel guidelines and firm style. Block-billing, caught early. When an entry breaks the rules, Celeste flags it and helps you either split it or rewrite the narrative. Analytics that connect the dots. Celeste pulls together work activity, billing rules, and financial data to show what’s driving realization, matter economics, utilization, and AI tool performance. These solutions mark Intapp’s shift to an agent-first platform. Intake, Conflicts, Terms, and Time no longer just support human-led work; Celeste now carries that work forward with people stepping in where judgment matters most. Each solution runs on the same foundation of structured data, agentic workflows, systems of record, context, and guardrails, which is what lets Celeste do real work inside regulated processes. Intapp calls this approach Firm AI – agentic AI applied to the business of the firm itself, not just to individual tasks or work products. Availability Firms already running their business acceptance, time, and billing with Intapp can upgrade to the new agentic AI offerings. Once the new entitlement is activated, the new capabilities will be available in their existing environments. To see them in action, firms can book a demo or talk to their Intapp account team at intapp.com . Supporting quotes Thad Jampol, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer, Intapp “Intapp is now agent-first. We’ve re-architected our Compliance and Time solutions with Celeste and agentic workflows at their core, so the agents, the data they run on, and the compliance guardrails all come from one place. Pulling that together is the hard part, and it’s the part no one else has done. That’s what makes Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste real for firms – the agents do meaningful work inside regulated processes, on each firm’s own data and under its own rules.” Katherine Lowry, Chief Information Officer and Head of IncuBaker, BakerHostetler “There is really no true beginning or end to a workday in a law firm. Knowing that Celeste is there all the time is key. We believe that Celeste can have a very positive impact on our intake and conflicts process. Celeste’s cutting-edge AI capabilities will help us responsibly take on matters and evaluate conflicts faster than ever before. At BakerHostetler, we have experienced tremendous lateral growth in recent years and as a result, have onboarded a significant number of important new clients and complex engagements. We believe that Celeste will help us operate more efficiently as we continue to grow.” Additional resources Explore Intapp Celeste Learn more about Intapp Compliance Learn more about Intapp Time Connect with Intapp Learn more at Intapp Get more news in the Intapp newsroom Follow Intapp on LinkedIn Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains express and implied “forward-looking statements” within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including statements regarding Intapp’s products and services and the expected results or benefits from use of our products and services. summary: Benchling published BenchBench-Protocol, a benchmark testing if LLMs can troubleshoot wet lab protocols like expert scientists. Top models still miss the practical judgment lab work requires, showing a real gap between knowing biology and doing it.
body_text: Today, we’re publishing the results from BenchBench-Protocol , a benchmark built from thousands of real-world experiments that tests whether models can troubleshoot and optimize wet lab protocols like expert scientists. Read the paper here . LLMs know an extraordinary amount of biology. But knowing biology and doing biology are different things. A textbook can tell you how CRISPR works. It can’t teach you to troubleshoot a CRISPR protocol when cells die after transfection. We’ve spent the last year bringing AI to scientists across academia and industry. While there’s universal excitement for AI, the gap is clear. AI needs to get better at reasoning like an expert scientist in the lab. Today, LLMs are often evaluated on general reasoning and scientific knowledge, not the problems scientists actually face in the lab. That seam between the digital and the physical worlds is where we are focused. We recently built a team focused on evaluating and improving LLMs in wet lab biology. We are publishing the first in a series of benchmarks so model developers have a goal to improve on and scientists can choose models that best fit their work. BenchBench-Protocol Debugging and optimizing protocols is a challenge scientists face every day. Scientists start from a published protocol for a new technique they’re trying to use. They get it to work in their lab through repeated trial and error: adjusting it for different instruments, swapping reagents for ones they already have, tuning incubation times and concentrations. We wanted to measure how well LLMs reason through these problems. We collaborated with scientific experts to study thousands of real-world experiments. We identified the optimizations scientists made to protocols to get them to work, had them reviewed by multiple experts, and then turned them into tasks for an LLM. Opus 5 performs the best on BenchBench-Protocol at 59.2%, followed by GPT 5.6 at 47.1%. Kimi K3 performs surprisingly well among open source models at 45.7%. The failure modes point to gaps in the practical reasoning that makes an expert successful in the lab. Models give answers that sound sensible on paper but miss how experiments actually behave: assuming a measurement translates directly to a result without considering calibration, treating a sample as pure despite visible evidence it isn’t, or missing subtle changes in physical technique that can ruin an experiment. These gaps are unsurprising given what LLMs have been trained on. To get better, models need to learn not just from the clean results in published papers, but from real experiments and their messy outcomes. Supporting the ecosystem Reinforcement learning has made models dramatically better in other domains like coding: give them thousands of tasks, tell them whether their answers work, and they learn better ways to reason. We believe the same thing can happen in biology. Careful engineering can turn messy scientific data into tasks for models to attempt, learn from, and be evaluated against. We’ve learned a lot about how to do this well: finding tasks that capture real scientific judgment, separating idiosyncratic decisions from sound scientific reasoning, and developing rubrics that can reliably tell the difference. We’re now scaling this work up to increasingly difficult problems, from sequence design and recommending the next experiment all the way up to critical drug program decisions. Rigorous evaluations have become essential to how model labs improve frontier models. We expect they’ll become increasingly important to biopharma too, as companies look to understand how well AI can reason about their own science. If you’re interested in evaluating and improving AI for your own company, we’re happy to help. Get in touch here .

title: Cardiologist Shares 6 Night-Time Habits to Avoid for Better Heart Health

body_text: Heart health is influenced by more than just diet and exercise. What you do in the evening before going to sleep can also play an important role in supporting your cardiovascular system. A cardiologist has highlighted several common night-time habits that many people follow without realising they may place extra strain on the heart. These include activities linked to sleep quality, blood pressure control, stress levels, and the body’s natural recovery process. Cardiovascular disease remains one of the leading health concerns worldwide. In the UK alone, millions of people are living with heart and circulatory conditions, making prevention and daily lifestyle choices increasingly important. According to cardiology experts, making small adjustments after 6pm could help support healthier blood vessels, better sleep, and improved overall wellbeing. 1. Avoid Strong Antibacterial Mouthwash Before Bed Many people use mouthwash as part of their nightly hygiene routine, but some strong antibacterial products may affect the balance of bacteria in the mouth. The bacteria found naturally in the mouth play a role in converting certain compounds from food into nitric oxide. Nitric oxide helps blood vessels relax and maintain healthy circulation. Some powerful antibacterial mouthwashes may remove both harmful and beneficial bacteria. This could potentially reduce nitric oxide production and influence blood vessel function. While mouthwash can still be useful when recommended by a dentist, experts suggest avoiding unnecessary overuse of very strong antibacterial formulas, especially as part of a bedtime routine. Maintaining good oral health through regular brushing, flossing, and dental check-ups remains essential for both mouth and heart health. 2. Reduce Blue Light Exposure in the Evening Scrolling on a phone or watching screens in bed has become a normal habit for many people. However, exposure to bright blue light late at night can interfere with the body’s natural sleep cycle. Blue light can reduce melatonin production. Melatonin is best known as a hormone that helps regulate sleep, but it also has antioxidant properties that support the body. Poor sleep and reduced melatonin levels may contribute to increased stress levels and inflammation, factors that can affect cardiovascular health over time. To support better sleep, experts recommend reducing screen use before bedtime, lowering brightness settings, or switching to warmer lighting during the evening. Creating a relaxing bedtime environment can help the body move into recovery mode, allowing the heart and other organs to rest properly. 3. Avoid Intense Late-Night Exercise Exercise is one of the best ways to protect heart health, but timing and intensity can matter. High-intensity static exercises such as long planks, wall sits, or demanding strength movements may temporarily increase blood pressure and keep the nervous system activated. After a stressful day, the body may already be experiencing higher levels of tension. A tough workout late at night could make it harder to relax before sleep. Instead, experts recommend completing intense workouts earlier in the day when possible. Gentle evening activities such as walking, stretching, or light mobility exercises may be more suitable before bedtime. The goal is to encourage relaxation rather than stimulate the body when it should be preparing for rest. 4. Be Careful With Evening Supplements Many people use supplements or calming drinks as part of their night-time routine. While some products may support relaxation, they are not always suitable for everyone. Ingredients such as L-theanine, commonly found in green tea, can influence the nervous system. Because the nervous system and heart rhythm are closely connected, supplements may affect people differently depending on dosage, timing, and individual health conditions. Natural does not always mean risk-free. Anyone taking medication or managing a heart condition should speak with a healthcare professional before regularly using supplements. A balanced diet, good sleep habits, and healthy lifestyle choices often provide the foundation for supporting heart health. 5. Avoid Prolonged Breath Holding Exercises Breathing exercises are often promoted as a way to reduce stress and improve relaxation. When performed correctly, gentle breathing techniques can be beneficial for many people. However, repeatedly holding your breath for long periods may place additional stress on the cardiovascular system in some individuals. Extended breath holding can temporarily affect oxygen levels and create extra demands on the heart. People with existing heart or circulation problems should be particularly cautious with intense breathing practices. Simple slow breathing exercises that encourage relaxation are generally considered a safer approach for improving calmness before sleep. 6. Stop Eating Too Close to Bedtime Late-night meals are common, especially for people with busy schedules. However, eating shortly before sleep may affect the body’s ability to fully rest. When you eat close to bedtime, your digestive system remains active when your body should be moving into recovery mode. Experts suggest leaving several hours between your final meal and going to sleep. This may help improve digestion, support healthier blood pressure patterns, and allow the cardiovascular system to recover overnight. A lighter evening meal and an earlier dinner time may be helpful for people looking to improve sleep quality and overall health. Small Evening Changes Can Support Long-Term Heart Health Protecting your heart does not require major lifestyle changes overnight. Simple adjustments to daily routines can make a meaningful difference over time. Reducing late-night screen exposure, avoiding unnecessary stress before sleep, choosing appropriate exercise timing, and creating healthy eating habits are practical steps that may support cardiovascular wellbeing. However, everyone’s health situation is different. People with existing heart conditions, high blood pressure, or concerns about symptoms should always seek advice from a qualified medical professional. Conclusion The hours before bedtime are an important part of your daily health routine. According to cardiology advice, avoiding certain habits after 6pm may help the body relax, recover, and maintain healthier heart function. From limiting blue light exposure to avoiding heavy late-night meals, small lifestyle changes can support better sleep and cardiovascular health. Your evening routine is not just about preparing for tomorrow. It is also about giving your heart the opportunity to recover today. Sources Daily Mirror health, published July 2026. General cardiovascular health guidance from recognised medical organisations, including information on sleep, exercise, nutrition, and heart disease prevention. Research literature on nitric oxide, oral bacteria, sleep hormones, and cardiovascular function. Disclaimer This article is for informational purposes only and does not replace professional medical advice. Health recommendations may vary depending on individual circumstances, medical history, medications, and existing conditions. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional before making significant changes to your diet, exercise routine, supplements, or medical care.

title: Closing Health Equity Gaps With Language Access
summary: Health equity requires more than equal care. See how language access programs close care gaps in August 2026.
body_text: In most U.S. health systems, a patient's primary language, income, and zip code still predict whether they get diagnosed on time and whether they understand their treatment. That gap has a name. Health equity is the state in which everyone has a fair and just opportunity to attain their highest level of health, and reaching it requires removing the historical injustices, social determinants, and systemic barriers that produce unequal outcomes in the first place. For care delivery leaders, the most immediate lever is language. Your quality data already shows it: break down readmissions or missed follow-ups by preferred language and a pattern appears. Closing that gap is what a real language access program looks like. TLDR: Health equity means your patient's language, income, or zip code should not predict their outcome. 1 in 3 adults with limited English proficiency report language barriers blocked their understanding of care instructions, per KFF. A review of 281,000+ surgical patients found limited English proficiency linked to longer stays and higher skilled nursing facility discharge rates. Section 1557's 2024 final rule requires free, qualified interpreter services from any federally funded organization; unqualified bilingual staff alone does not satisfy it. Opalite Health is a physician-led AI medical interpreter covering 150+ languages, validated in an independent Johns Hopkins Medicine study. What health equity means Health equity is the absence of unfair, avoidable differences in health among population groups defined by social, economic, demographic, or geographic characteristics. Put plainly, it means a patient's income, race, primary language, or zip code should not predict whether they get diagnosed on time or understand their treatment. Reaching it takes more than handing every patient the same appointment. Two patients can receive identical care and walk away with different outcomes when one cannot read the discharge instructions or afford the follow-up, a pattern documented in health equity outcomes for LEP patients . For care delivery leaders, the concept sets the standard: close the gaps in access, communication, and follow-through that produce worse results for specific groups, then fix the structural causes underneath them. Closing those gaps also means looking backward. Structural racism, discriminatory policies, and unequal resource distribution have compounded over generations, well beyond a few years. The WHO and CDC both frame health equity as a human rights obligation, not a courtesy, meaning equitable access is owed to every patient regardless of circumstances. Those historical roots are what show up today as the language, income, and geographic gaps described throughout this article. Health equity vs health equality vs health disparity Three terms get used interchangeably, though they describe different things. Term Definition Example in Care Delivery Health Equality Treating every patient identically: same resources, same process. Handing every patient the same English discharge instructions. Health Equity Matching resources to need so each patient has a fair shot at their best outcome. Providing discharge instructions in the patient's primary language. Health Disparity The measurable gap in outcomes that appears when equity is missing. Higher readmission rates for patients with limited English proficiency who received English-only instructions. Picture a clinic handing the same English discharge instructions to every patient leaving the emergency department. That is equality. Every patient gets the identical document. But a patient with limited English proficiency cannot act on instructions they cannot read, so their readmission risk climbs. The gap between that patient's outcome and an English-speaking patient's outcome is the disparity, sometimes called a health inequity when it is avoidable and unfair. Social determinants of health and their role in care gaps Social determinants of health are the non-medical conditions that shape whether a patient stays well: income, education, employment, housing stability, and the language they speak at home. These structural factors, not genetics or individual choices alone, drive most of the disparities seen across racial, ethnic, geographic, and linguistic groups. The CDC estimates that social determinants account for up to 50% of health outcomes. Income and wealth: lower household income tied to higher rates of unmanaged chronic disease. Educational attainment: lower literacy linked to reduced health knowledge and preventive care use. Employment and working conditions: unstable or hazardous work raises exposure to injury and stress-related illness. Housing stability: linked to higher rates of untreated chronic disease and avoidable ED visits. Food security: diet-related conditions such as diabetes disproportionately affect food-insecure populations. Transportation access: lack of reliable transit a leading reason patients miss scheduled appointments. Language and literacy: limited English proficiency creates a structural barrier to understanding and acting on care instructions. The WHO World Report on Health Equity , launched in May 2025, confirmed that health and well-being depend on far more than access to care, and that avoidable gaps shrink only when these non-medical root causes are tackled. Language sits squarely in this list. A patient who cannot understand their care plan faces a structural barrier every bit as real as an unpaid rent notice. Health inequity examples in the United States These are the disparities that surface when equity fails. Each has its own drivers. Racial and ethnic disparities in mortality Life expectancy and disease burden still vary sharply across racial and ethnic groups, driven by structural racism, uneven access, and economic inequality. Black Americans have a life expectancy roughly 4 years lower than white Americans, according to CDC 2023 data. Socioeconomic barriers to preventive care Lower-income patients receive fewer screenings and lean on the emergency department for care earlier intervention could have prevented. Adults in the lowest income quartile are 2 to 3 times less likely to receive recommended cancer screenings, per the AHRQ National Healthcare Quality Report. Geographic inequity and rural access Rural patients contend with fewer providers, longer travel, and thin specialist coverage. Rural counties have roughly 40% fewer primary care physicians per capita than urban counties, according to HRSA data. Language access as a health inequity About one in three adults with limited English proficiency reported that language barriers made it hard to understand a provider's instructions, per KFF survey findings . Mental health care disparities Underserved communities carry higher unmet mental health needs, compounded by stigma, provider shortages, and cost. Only 1 in 3 racial and ethnic minority adults with a mental illness receives treatment, compared with about 1 in 2 in the general population, per SAMHSA. Disability-related care gaps People with disabilities meet barriers across facility design, communication, and informed consent. Adults with disabilities are twice as likely to report forgoing needed medical care due to cost, according to CDC data. How language barriers drive health inequities When a patient cannot communicate with their care team, the failure moves through predictable clinical stages. Histories come back incomplete. Symptoms get misread. Consent gets signed without real understanding; medications get taken wrong, and follow-up plans go unfollowed. Satisfaction drops because the patient never felt heard. The surgical evidence makes the pattern concrete. A systematic review of 29 studies covering more than 281,000 patients found that surgical patients with limited English proficiency had reduced access to care, longer hospital admissions, and higher rates of discharge to skilled nursing facilities than English-proficient patients. Language rarely travels alone. It clusters with lower income, thinner insurance coverage, and reduced health literacy, so each barrier deepens the others. The legal and policy framework for language access Language access in U.S. healthcare is a legal duty, not a courtesy. Two federal authorities anchor it. Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 bars discrimination based on national origin, which regulators read to include failing to provide meaningful access for patients with limited English proficiency in any federally funded program, with federal language access requirements spelling out what that means in practice. Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act sharpens that duty. The 2024 final rule, effective July 5, 2024, requires covered entities to offer timely, accurate, free language assistance from qualified interpreters, bars reliance on unqualified bilingual staff as interpreters , and mandates written policies plus annual notices in each state's 15 most common languages. Any organization taking federal financial assistance, including Medicare and Medicaid, is bound. The rule also reaches machine translation: when AI-powered translation touches critical rights, human review applies under certain conditions. How language access programs close health care gaps Closing care gaps takes a layered program built in phases: start with data and needs assessment, then layer in interpreter services, patient materials, staffing, and training. Data-driven needs assessment: tracking demand by department and shift lets you allocate resources and catch coverage gaps early. Qualified interpreter services (in-person, video, audio): the standard for high-acuity and complex conversations, though limited by connection time, rare language interpreter gaps , and per-minute cost. AI interpretation for LEP patients : instant access across many languages, a strong first-line option for routine and lower-acuity encounters, with escalation to a qualified human interpreter for acute psychiatric crises or at the patient's request; for guidance on sensitive scenarios see palliative care language access . Plain language in patient materials : translated discharge instructions and after-visit summaries lift comprehension and medication adherence. Language-concordant staffing: matching bilingual staff and community health workers to high-need populations builds trust, an approach grounded in cultural humility for language access , and steadies chronic disease management. Staff training and workflow integration: access only helps when providers can start it fast and know which encounters to escalate. Each layer addresses a distinct failure point in the care journey, from first contact through discharge, so gaps close systematically rather than ad hoc. Measuring progress toward language access and health equity Equity work is measurable. Stratify existing quality data by preferred language first, then track: Access: time to interpretation, language coverage, and documented interpretation per encounter with limited English proficiency. Clinical: readmissions, medication adherence, and discharge comprehension by language. Experience: HCAHPS scores and satisfaction by preferred language. Financial: interpretation cost per encounter and avoidable ED use. How Opalite Health supports language access as a health equity strategy We built Opalite Health to close the communication gap running through every disparity described above. It is a physician-led AI medical interpreter designed for clinical conversations, not consumer translation, with real-time spoken interpretation across more than 150 languages and dialects, including 8 Spanish dialects. Because it is available instantly and around the clock, it reduces connection delays that drive care gaps. In an independent Johns Hopkins Medicine validation study comparing Opalite with certified medical interpreters, Opalite produced more than 90% fewer major and critical errors. Opalite Guardian, our quality and safety framework, flags hallucinations, omissions, negation errors, and clinically meaningful mistranslations in real time. Opalite is HIPAA compliant, supports Business Associate Agreements, and integrates with leading EHRs including Epic, Cerner, eClinicalWorks, and athenahealth. It works within a risk-based language access program alongside qualified human interpreters, giving hospitals, health systems, FQHCs, and community health centers a way to act on the equity commitments this post describes. Final thoughts on building health equity through language access Health equity is the state in which every patient has a fair and just opportunity to reach their best health outcome regardless of language, income, or zip code. Getting there in practice runs through three levers: legal compliance with language access obligations, program design that accounts for social determinants, and technology that closes communication gaps at the point of care. None of those levers works as a one-time fix. Progress requires ongoing measurement, stratified by language and population, so gaps surface before they compound. See Opalite Health in action .

title: Market Metrics That Matter: European Equities July Volume Briefing
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_text: Welcome to the July edition of Market Metrics That Matter, your monthly briefing on European cash equities trends. Don’t forget to visit Cboe Europe’s Market Share page for leading insights into European equity trading activity. July 2026 Highlights European equity trading volumes continued to soften in July, following the high-volatility start to the year, with activity shifting from Closing Auctions toward Central Limit Order Books and Non-Displayed venues. Total on-exchange average daily value traded (ADVT) reached €57.5bn, down 11% on June but up 23% year-on-year. Total addressable activity (on- and off-exchange) stood at €80bn, versus €93.2bn in June, though still up 21% on July 2025. With no major index expiries or rebalances in play, activity shifted into continuous trading and away from Closing Auctions, which fell to 24.3% of on-exchange activity versus 27.9% in June. Central Limit Order Books grew to 52.8% of on-exchange activity (from 50.1% in June); Periodic Auctions rose to 10.4% (from 9.7%); and non-displayed order books moved to 10.9% (from 10.2%). Systematic Internaliser (SI) activity contracted slightly but continued its year-on-year growth trend. Addressable SI ADVT came in at €14.3bn (vs €17.6bn in June), representing 17.8% of total addressable volume - down from 18.8% in June, but up from 15.1% in July 2025. Zurich-listed securities posted the strongest month-on-month gain in market share (+0.6pp), while Frankfurt saw the largest decline (-1pp). Cboe Europe remained the largest equities exchange by market share, driven by its strong mix of trading mechanisms. Cboe Europe's overall market share rose to 24.37%, up from 23.15% in June - making it both the largest pan-European stock exchange and the biggest market share gainer of the month. Cboe BIDS Europe, Cboe's European block trading platform, held the top position in the block segment for a 52nd consecutive month, posting a monthly ADVT of €653.3 million and an above-LIS market share of 34% - its highest level since May 2024. Cboe ranked number one in non-displayed trading, including reference price waiver and large-in-scale activity, with a 41.7% segment market share, and in Periodic Auctions (75.5% share). title: Apple Ads Beginner’s Guide: Using the $100 Credit
summary: Apple Ads (formerly Apple Search Ads) puts your app at the top of App Store search. Learn Basic vs. Advanced and how to spend the $100 credit wisely
body_text: You built your app, got it through App Review, and finally launched it on the App Store. Then you search for the exact problem your app solves…and your app is nowhere to be found. That’s normal for a brand-new app. It has no download history, few or no ratings, and very little data for the App Store to work with. So… now what? Apple Ads gives you a way to pay for visibility while you’re building that history. It’s Apple’s advertising platform for promoting apps inside the App Store. The most useful option for many new developers is a search results campaign, which can place your app in a prominent position when someone searches for a relevant term. As of August 2026, Apple also gives eligible new Apple Ads accounts a one-time $100 promotional credit . That isn’t enough to build a giant campaign, but it is enough to learn how the platform works, test a few keywords, and get some of your first downloads. Check the eligibility requirements . What are Apple Ads? Apple Ads lets developers advertise their apps across several locations in the App Store. You may still hear people call it Apple Search Ads , which was the platform’s previous name. Apple changed the name to Apple Ads in April 2025 as its advertising products expanded beyond search results. For a beginner, the basic idea is simple: A user opens the App Store. They search for an app that solves a specific problem. Your app appears as a clearly labeled ad within those results. You pay when the user taps the ad or with Apple Ads Basic, when the tap leads to an install. That search intent is what makes Apple Ads so valuable. Think about it. The person isn’t randomly scrolling through social media while you interrupt them with an ad. They’re already on the App Store actively searching for an app, using a search term you want to show up for. You’re reaching them at exactly the right moment. Why Apple Ads can be useful for a new app A new app has a discoverability problem. Even with good App Store Optimization , it's difficult to compete against established apps with years of downloads, ratings, reviews, and user activity. Apple Ads can help you generate initial traffic while you continue improving your product page and app experience. It’s also relatively simple compared with many other advertising platforms. You don’t need to film a stack of TikToks, design Facebook ads, or hire creators before you can run your first campaign. Apple builds the ad using the app name, icon, subtitle, screenshots, and other assets you’ve already uploaded through App Store Connect. Apple Ads can also teach you how people search for your app. If you discover that a specific keyword produces affordable downloads in a particular country, you can invest more heavily in that combination. Those insights may also improve your organic keyword strategy and product-page messaging. Apple Ads Basic vs. Advanced Apple offers two versions of its App Store advertising product: Apple Ads Basic and Apple Ads Advanced . Despite the name, Advanced is almost always the better option for an independent developer who wants to understand where their money is going. With Basic , you choose the app, target countries, monthly budget, and maximum amount you’re willing to pay for an install. Apple then decides which searches and users should see the app. That sounds convenient, but you lose a lot of valuable information. You can’t see or control the individual keywords receiving your budget, and the reporting is very limited. Advanced lets you choose the placement, country, keywords, match types, and individual keyword bids. It also provides highly detailed reporting so you can analyze which searches are actually producing taps and installs. You don’t need to be an expert to use Advanced. You can create a very simple Advanced campaign while keeping control over the decisions that matter. Feature Apple Ads Basic Apple Ads Advanced Campaign setup Apple automates most decisions You control placements, targeting, keywords, and bids Available placements Search results Today tab, Search tab, search results, and product pages Keyword control No keyword selection Manual keyword control with Manage Bids Pricing model Cost per install Cost per tap Budget Monthly budget Daily campaign budget Reporting Simplified dashboard Detailed campaign, keyword, and search-term reporting Best for Minimal management Learning, testing, and optimizing performance Where can Apple Ads appear? Apple Ads Advanced currently supports four App Store placements. All four can be useful in a very large marketing strategy, but Search Results is far and away the most impactful for new developers and those without million dollar ad budgets. Today tab The Today tab is the App Store’s front page. An ad here can generate broad awareness, but the person hasn’t necessarily shown an interest in your app’s category. This is a prominent placement, but it probably isn’t where I would spend a small first-time budget. Search tab A Search tab ad appears at the top of the suggested apps list before the user enters a search. The person has at least opened the Search tab, but you still don’t know what they plan to search for. It’s more targeted than general awareness advertising, but less targeted than advertising against a specific query. Search results Search results ads appear after someone enters a query. Your ad can appear at the top of the results or farther down the page. This is the bread and butter placement for a small beginner campaign because you can target people based on what they’re actively searching for. You can’t buy a particular position. Apple decides whether the ad appears and where it appears based on factors that include your bid and how relevant your app is to the search. Throwing a huge bid at an unrelated keyword won’t make an irrelevant app appear. Here's how ads are matched with search queries on the App Store. Product pages Product-page ads appear near the bottom of another app’s listing, at the top of the You Might Also Like section. These ads can reach people who are comparing apps in a particular category, but they don’t give you the same direct keyword intent as a search results campaign. How do Apple Ads keywords work? When you create an Advanced search results campaign, Apple currently offers two bid strategies: Manage Bids and Maximize Conversions . Manage Bids Manage Bids lets you choose your keywords and set the maximum amount you’re willing to pay for a tap on each one. This is the option I would use for a tightly controlled $100 experiment. You can select a small group of relevant keywords, monitor the results, and understand exactly what you’re testing. Maximize Conversions Maximize Conversions uses an automated bidder and Search Match to try to generate the most installs around a target cost per acquisition. It may be useful once you have more data and a larger ongoing budget. However, Search Match is required in its automated ad group, and you can’t manage individual keyword bids there. For a small first campaign where the goal is to learn, Manage Bids gives you more control. Exact match vs. broad match Apple Ads supports two keyword match types: Exact match gives you tighter control. Your ad is matched to the specific keyword and what Apple considers close variations, which can include misspellings, reordered words, and other closely related versions. If you're on a tight budget, you want to use exact match. Broad match lets Apple match your keyword to a larger group of related searches. This can help you discover new terms, but it can also spread a small budget across searches you didn’t expect. This is helpful if you have the budget to experiment. What is Search Match? Search Match allows Apple to automatically match your ad with searches based on information such as your App Store metadata, similar apps, and other search data. It can be helpful for keyword discovery if you have the budget to experiment. If you're on a tight ad budget, turn Search Match off and use a deliberate list of exact-match keywords. That prevents your budget from being spent on experimentation before you understand the basics. How to use the Apple Ads $100 credit The goal of your first $100 campaign shouldn’t be to scale your entire app business. To be honest, $100 is nothing when it comes to an ad budget. The goal should be to learn which keywords and countries show signs of working and to get your first batch of downloads and users. Here’s a simple starting strategy to maximize your $100 free credit. 1. Confirm that you qualify for the credit Apple says you must be the registered App Store Connect Account Holder, have at least one app available on the App Store in an eligible market, and link your top-level Apple Ads account to App Store Connect. You’ll also need to add a valid payment method. Check the Billing page to confirm that the credit has been applied before launching your campaign. 🚨 One important warning : Apple won’t notify you when the credit is exhausted. If your campaign spends more than the promotional balance, the additional amount is charged to your payment method. Set an end date, monitor the campaign, and check your invoices. Apple’s promotional-credit terms explain these conditions . 2. Use Apple Ads Advanced Choose an Advanced search results campaign with the Manage Bids strategy. That gives you control over the keywords, match types, bids, and country being tested. 3. Target one country Don’t split $100 among ten countries. You’ll end up with tiny amounts of data everywhere and not enough information to make a decision anywhere. If your app only supports English, you might test Canada, Australia, or the United Kingdom rather than immediately entering a highly competitive U.S. auction. (The U.S. will typically be the most expensive keywords to bid on). Another option is to localize the app and test a specific non-English market. For example, you could translate the app and App Store product page into French and run French keywords in France. Advertising costs vary by category, keyword, and market, so there’s no guarantee that one country will always be cheaper. The point is to run a focused test rather than spreading your budget too thin. With Apple ads, you should always be running small tests to figure out what works. 4. Choose a small set of long-tail keywords A broad keyword such as meal planner could attract a lot of competition and may include users with very different needs. A keyword like this will rapidly drain your $100 credit. More specific searches might include: family meal planner weekly meal planner for families gluten free meal planner meal planner with grocery list meal planner for picky eaters These keywords will usually have less search volume, but the intent is clearer. Someone searching for a gluten-free meal planner is telling you exactly what they want. Start with a handful of highly relevant terms rather than hundreds of loosely related keywords. These long-tail keywords are almost always much cheaper. 5. Use exact match Set the keywords to exact match so your initial budget stays focused on the searches you intentionally selected. You can experiment with broad match later when you have more money for keyword discovery. 6. Turn off Search Match For this specific test, turn off Search Match so Apple doesn’t automatically expand the campaign to additional queries. 7. Use a conservative daily budget and an end date Choose a daily budget that prevents the credit from disappearing in one afternoon. A starting range such as $5 to $10 per day can give you time to monitor what’s happening, although the right amount depends on your keyword bids and available search volume. Set an end date and check the campaign regularly. Apple Ads campaigns can continue spending until you pause them or they reach their scheduled end. Fix your product page before buying traffic Apple Ads can put your app in front of someone. It can’t make them tap or download. Before spending anything, make sure your App Store listing is in a solid place (especially your icon, subtitle, and first few screenshots). Your screenshots should immediately answer three questions: What does this app do? Who is it for? Why should I download it instead of the other results? If the screenshots are confusing, cluttered, or focused on unimportant features, your ad won't get many taps. The same principle applies after the download. You’re paying to bring someone into the app, so the onboarding and first-time experience need to be clear. Don’t lose a paid user behind an unnecessary sign-up screen, confusing permissions request, or broken onboarding flow. Before starting your campaign, review the Bitrig guide to App Store Optimization and make sure the product page is ready to convert attention into downloads. How should you judge the first campaign? Don’t evaluate a $100 test only by asking, “How many downloads did I get?” Look at what you learned. Useful Apple Ads metrics include: Impressions: How many times the ad appeared Taps: How many people tapped it Tap-through rate: The percentage of impressions that became taps Installs: How many attributed downloads resulted Conversion rate: The percentage of taps that became installs Average cost per tap: How much each tap cost Cost per acquisition: How much you spent for each attributed install A keyword with many impressions but very few taps may not match your app’s positioning. A keyword with taps but no installs may indicate that your product page isn’t meeting the expectation created by the search. A keyword that consistently produces affordable installs is worth investigating further. You might raise its bid, test it in another country, or create screenshots and messaging that align more closely with that specific intent. Even a small campaign can give you useful information about how real customers describe the problem your app solves. Frequently asked questions about Apple Ads Is Apple Ads the same as Apple Search Ads? Yes. Apple Search Ads was renamed Apple Ads in April 2025. The current Apple Ads platform covers App Store search advertising as well as other placements across Apple services. Does every new account receive a $100 credit? No. The credit is for eligible new accounts. Apple currently requires the account to be linked correctly to App Store Connect, with the registered Account Holder and at least one app available in an eligible App Store market. The offer and its terms may change, so check Apple’s official promotional-credit page before creating the campaign. Should a beginner choose Apple Ads Basic or Advanced? Advanced is usually the better choice for a developer who wants to learn from the campaign. Basic is easier to set up, but it doesn’t provide keyword selection or keyword-level data. Advanced with Manage Bids can still be kept simple while giving you much more control. How much does Apple Ads cost? There is no fixed price for a keyword. In Apple Ads Advanced, you set the maximum cost-per-tap bid you’re willing to pay. The actual cost depends on factors such as competition, your bid, and your app’s relevance to the search. Apple Ads Basic uses a cost-per-install model instead. Do I need to create separate ad graphics? Not necessarily. Apple can create ads from the metadata and assets already on your App Store product page. Advanced campaigns can also use custom product pages and ad variations when you want your screenshots and messaging to align with a particular audience or keyword theme. Can I guarantee that my app appears in the first position? No. Search results ads can appear at the top or farther down the page, and advertisers can’t select or bid for one exact position. Apple considers both the bid and the app’s relevance to the search query. Will Apple Ads improve my organic App Store ranking? Not automatically. Buying ads doesn’t guarantee that your app will move higher in the unpaid results. Ads can help you attract initial users, test keyword demand, get app ratings, and improve your understanding of the market. Those benefits may indirectly support your broader growth and ASO strategy, but paid placement and organic ranking aren’t the same thing. The bottom line Apple Ads is one of the most direct ways to put a new app in front of people who are already searching the App Store for something similar. For a first campaign, keep it simple: use Apple Ads Advanced, choose the search results placement, select Manage Bids, target one country, start with a small group of exact-match keywords, and turn off Search Match. Just make sure your screenshots, product page, and first-time user experience are ready before paying to send people there. The $100 promotional credit won’t build your entire app business, but it can help you earn some initial downloads and learn how real customers search for an app like yours. Try Bitrig When you’re ready to build and launch your app, Bitrig helps new developers create native, high-quality Swift apps with AI. You can focus on turning your idea into a real app, then use tools such as App Store Optimization and Apple Ads to help people discover it.
