title: 7 Plumbing field service software tools worth using
summary: Struggling to keep plumbing jobs organized? We compare 7 plumbing field service software tools to help you find the right fit.
body_text: It’s 2 a.m., and your phone won’t stop buzzing. One customer has a burst pipe, another has a water heater flooding their basement, and you’ve already got three jobs booked for one truck tomorrow. For a growing plumbing business, that’s not a bad day. It’s a Tuesday. A basic scheduling app can put those jobs on a calendar. But once you’re running a few trucks, you need more than that. You need to know: Who called and what happened on their last visit Which plumber is free Whether their last invoice‌ was paid That’s where plumbing business software comes in. It makes it possible to handle scheduling, dispatch, customer records, and payments, and do it all from one place. We looked at plumbing field service software for different team sizes and types of work. We narrowed the list down to seven options. Here’s a quick look at what we found: The best plumbing field service software for small and growing businesses is Jobber . The best option for plumbing-specific integrations is Housecall Pro . The best option for project-based and commercial plumbing work is Knowify . The best option for larger plumbing operations is ServiceTitan . In addition to an in-depth comparison, you’ll also find a guide on how to pick the right tool and what features to look for. 7 Best plumbing service software researched and ranked Below is a comparison of the seven best field service software for plumbing businesses. We’ve included options built for small and growing teams, along with a few worth considering as your business scales. 7 Top plumbing service management software compared Here’s an overview of the best plumbing field service software on the market: Tool Best for Standout features Starting price Jobber Small and growing plumbing businesses Client hub, GPS dispatching and route optimization, Quo phone integration $29 per month, solo plan Housecall Pro Field service-specific integrations Native flat-rate price book, Profit Rhino integration, consumer financing $59 per month, single user Service Fusion Flat-rate pricing for unlimited users Unlimited users at one flat rate, built-in GPS fleet tracking, dispatch zones Custom pricing FieldPulse Automating workflows Fully customizable job workflows, truck-level inventory tracking, live map view Custom pricing FieldEdge Native maintenance agreement management 30,000+ pre-built plumbing repairs, equipment history by property, automated renewal reminders Custom pricing Knowify Job costing and project-based plumbing work Job budgeting and costing, AIA-style progress billing, two-way QuickBooks sync $99 per month, one user ServiceTitan Large plumbing companies AI-based route optimization, full customer history on incoming calls, marketing ROI tracking Custom pricing 1. Jobber: Best plumbing field service software for small and growing businesses Pros Easy to use across office and field Quick onboarding, often in as little as a day Smooth quote-to-invoice-to-payment flow Centralized scheduling for the entire team Cons Mobile app is more limited than the desktop version Features like expense tracking cost extra on higher tiers No built-in flat-rate price book Jobber is field service management software and CRM for plumbers. It keeps customer details, job history, and communication in one place. It also lets you manage everything from quoting and scheduling to invoicing and job analysis.Every team plan comes with GPS tracking and route optimization. So when you get an emergency call for a burst pipe, you can see which plumber is closest and get them there by the fastest route. Once you dispatch them, your crew can check the customer’s job history, update the job status, and add repair notes from the Jobber mobile app. When the job’s done, they can send the invoice and collect payment on-site. Customers can also approve quotes and pay invoices through Jobber’s client portal. Here’s how one business owner described the experience: “J obber helps automate our schedule – which is quite busy. I love the professional quoting, follow-ups, and email/text reminders. The invoicing has been a time saver as well. Customer service is great .” — G2 Jobber also integrates with Quo, a phone system for home service businesses . After a customer call, Quo sends the summary and transcript to their Jobber record. So whoever takes over the job can quickly see what the customer said and what they need. Need to call the customer back? You can do it right from their Jobber contact card using the built-in click-to-call feature. Tap their phone number, and Quo places the call using your main business number. If your team is unavailable to pick up, turn on Sona , Quo’s plumbing answering service , to handle calls 24/7. Sona follows your custom instructions to collect the caller’s details, equipment issue, and job urgency. You can also instruct it to set up a service request on Jobber based on the conversation and your requirements. Key features of Jobber Client hub GPS dispatching and route optimization Good, better, best quoting for repair options Automated review requests QuickBooks integration Jobber pricing Jobber’s individual plan starts at $21 per month for the first year, and $29 per month afterwards. This makes it accessible for solo plumbers transitioning from spreadsheets. For plumbing businesses with two to five employees, Jobber offers three team plans: Connect: $149 per month for up to five users for job scheduling and dispatching, GPS route optimization, quotes and invoices, automated client reminders, checklists, workflow automations, and QuickBooks Online sync Grow: $229 per month for up to five users for job costing and profitability tracking, automatic time tracking, advanced quote customization, lead management, and high-value quote alerts Plus: $399 per month for up to five users for an AI receptionist, Marketing Suite, API access, dedicated onboarding, and premium support 2. Housecall Pro: Best for field service-specific integrations Pros Full quote-to-invoice-to-payment flow in one place Third-party integrations with CompanyCam and Profit Rhino Native flat-rate price book for plumbing Available in Spanish and English Cons No built-in map view when scheduling jobs Adding users requires a plan upgrade Limited customization for plumbing-specific workflows Housecall Pro leans more into the money side of plumbing work: pricing, job costing, and getting paid. Its base plan includes a price book to keep pricing consistent across your team. Upgrading to a higher tier adds job costing, along with good, better, best estimates for jobs like water heater replacements. You can also connect tools like Profit Rhino and The New Flat Rate to present flat-rate options and give customers more choice before a repair. On the dispatch side, GPS tracking helps route the nearest available plumber to an emergency call. Service agreements make recurring work like annual drain cleanings easier to manage. Have a bigger job on the books? Use progress invoicing to collect payments in stages. Keep in mind, Housecall Pro’s Basic plan is only built for a single user. Have more people on your team? You’ll have to upgrade to Essentials, even if you don’t need the extra features. One business owner ran into exactly that: “I do not like having to pay more to add more contractors. I would prefer to not do that, as I will be adding more over the next year, and it significantly increases my pricing.” — ​​G2 Key features of Housecall Pro Consumer financing for big-ticket jobs Review management Time tracking Membership plans for recurring customers Customer portal Housecall Pro pricing Housecall Pro requires you to fill out a form before seeing its pricing options. Once you do, you can choose between two options: plans for individuals, and plans for teams. Here’s what you’ll pay as an individual user: Basic: $79 per month for one user, CRM tools, invoices and payments, online booking, job cost tracking, offline viewing, and access to the mobile app Essentials: $229 per month for one user, QuickBooks Online, customer equipment tracking, employee GPS tracking, and checklists Max: $349 per month for one user, advanced custom reporting, a dedicated onboarding specialist, and escalated phone support Here’s what you’ll pay for a team: Essentials: $299 per month for five included users, the sales proposal tool, membership plans, equipment tracking, and QuickBooks sync Max: $ 649 per month for eight included users, pipeline, route optimization, pricing insights, open API access, dedicated onboarding specialist, and access to an account manager 3. Service Fusion: Best plumbing field service software with flat-rate pricing for unlimited users Pros Unlimited users for one flat monthly rate Built-in GPS fleet tracking Two-way QuickBooks sync Core features are included across all plans Cons Mobile app can be slow and prone to syncing issues No free trial available Lacks modern automation like smart dispatching Service Fusion’s pricing model works differently from most plumbing field service management software. Instead of paying per technician, you pay one flat rate for unlimited users. The Starter plan covers the day-to-day work of running a plumbing team. Service Fusion’s dispatch board shows technician availability and lets you drag and drop jobs as calls come in. You can also create dispatch zones and use GPS tracking to see where your plumbers are. Upgrade to the Plus plan, and you get inventory management, job costing, and photo uploads. Out in the field, plumbers can manage jobs from the Service Fusion mobile app. They can check customer details, create estimates, send invoices, and collect payments on-site. Service Fusion also connects with QuickBooks Online and Desktop. With another upgrade, you get voice and texting. But they’re fairly basic. They don’t include advanced call routing or automated follow-ups. That may be limiting if your plumbing business handles a lot of customer calls and texts. Some people also struggle with Service Fusion’s reliability: See for yourself: “Our senior team members are frequently on the road without access to a laptop. There are far too many functions the app cannot access. The texting functions show our personal phone numbers unless we are sending an On The Way text or at a laptop using the (very clunky) text functions there. The texting needs major improvements.” — Capterra Key features of Service Fusion Dispatch zones for territory-based routing Customer “track your tech” ETA view eSignatures on estimates In-field payment processing Service Fusion pricing Service Fusion doesn’t make pricing publicly available, so you’ll have to contact their sales team for a custom quote. Some users report flat rates starting at $208 per month . 4. FieldPulse: Best field service software for automating workflows Pros Truck-level inventory tracking with reorder alerts Booking portal Highly rated customer support Cons No transparent pricing available Reporting and customization can be limited Some users report a steep learning curve FieldPulse is a solid option for teams that want control and customizability over their workflows. For instance, you’re not locked into a fixed set of job stages. You can map out each step of a job using statuses like “waiting for parts” or “ready for invoice.” When a job reaches a certain stage, FieldPulse can automatically notify a warehouse manager or send the customer an update. You get these workflow tools even with the entry-level Essentials plan. Once a workflow is set up, plumbers can follow its steps and update job statuses from the mobile app. Take it from a business owner: “The interface is user-friendly, the mobile app keeps field teams connected, and the automation features help save time and reduce manual effort. Overall, it has helped streamline day-to-day operations and improve efficiency across the team.” — Capterra Just know FieldPulse doesn’t disclose their pricing. That means you won’t know how to estimate your software expenses without contacting their team. Key features of FieldPulse Custom forms Online booking portal Customer alerts and reminders Maintenance agreements Multi-location support FieldPulse pricing FieldPulse has three plans to choose from: Essentials: Includes customer management, scheduling and dispatching, work order management, estimates and invoices, a mobile app, and workflow automation Professional: Adds project management and QuickBooks sync Enterprise: Adds multi-location management and open API access Pricing isn’t listed publicly. You’ll need to contact their sales team for a custom quote based on your team size. 5. FieldEdge: Best for native maintenance agreement management Pros Real-time dispatch board Automated billing for recurring maintenance plans Integrated timesheets and time-tracking Cons Can be slow to load Some users struggle with QuickBooks setup No office-to-tech messaging FieldEdge is a good fit if you don’t want to build your plumbing price book from scratch. It comes with more than 30,000 pre-built plumbing repairs, including standard labor times and parts. Add your own labor rates and markups, and your plumbers can use the final prices to quote jobs in the field. The software also helps you manage maintenance agreements. You can track expiring agreements, upcoming renewals, and billing schedules in one place. Renewal notices go out automatically, too, reducing the need for manual follow-ups. But FieldEdge can take some time to get used to. Some users report a difficult onboarding process and problems with QuickBooks syncing. Inventory tracking may also be too basic if you want to keep tabs on parts across individual plumbing trucks. One business owner said: “ We got almost no support from Field Edge while using their software. We were often left to figure things out on our own. ” — Capterra Key features of FieldEdge Good-better-best quoting Customer notification system Two-way QuickBooks sync Equipment tracking by property Mobile access to schedules and payments FieldEdge pricing FieldEdge offers three plans for plumbing teams. Pricing isn’t public, so you’ll need to book a demo with their sales team before you can get a custom quote. Here’s the breakdown: Select: Booking and scheduling, dispatching, customer management and service history, technician time tracking, invoicing and payments, QuickBooks online and desktop sync, flat-rate pricing, and basic service agreements Premier: Advanced dispatching, advanced service agreements, multi-option quotes, prospect tracking, performance and commission tracking, saved reports, and additional mobile app licenses Elite: Professional sales proposal tools, unlimited saved reports, warehouse inventory management, outbound call recording, and a customer portal 6. Knowify: Best for job costing and project-based plumbing work Pros Job costing and progress billing AIA-style billing for commercial jobs Works offline in low-signal spots Responsive, hands-on customer support Cons Weaker dispatching than dispatch-first tools Inventory doesn’t sync with QuickBooks Solo plan is expensive Reporting and invoicing customization are limited Knowify is plumbing contractor software for businesses that take on longer, project-based jobs. Think repipes, remodels, and commercial installations that can run for days or weeks. Before work starts, you can build a budget for the job. As work progresses, you can track labor, materials, and other costs against that budget. This helps you spot jobs that are starting to run over budget. If the scope changes halfway through a job, you can create and track change orders. For commercial work, Knowify also supports progress billing, retainage, and AIA-style billing. The tool also has a two-way integration with QuickBooks Online. Create an invoice in Knowify, for example, and it syncs with QuickBooks. The reverse is also true. That said, reporting can be quite limited. Some users say they can’t build the reports they need and have to export the data to customize it elsewhere. One business owner highlighted the issue: “ Need a more robust reporting tool since we can only run preset reports and not able to have access to the entire data set for custom reporting” — G2 Key features of Knowify AIA billing Bidding and estimating Scheduling and dispatching Mobile time tracking Service asset and equipment tracking Client portal Knowify pricing Plumbing teams can choose from three Knowify plans: Core: $99 per month for one user and includes estimates and proposals, fixed-price and AIA billing, scheduling, time tracking, progress billing, payment processing, and QuickBooks Online sync Advanced: $329 per month for up to 10 users and adds project budgets, daily logs, work orders, a client portal, custom workflows, job costing, and real-time work-in-progress reporting Enterprise: Custom pricing for unlimited users and adds RFIs and submittals, document markup, prevailing wage support, and full inventory and equipment management 7. ServiceTitan: Best for large plumbing companies Pros AI-powered scheduling optimization and route planning Advanced payment processing tools, including Tap to Pay Open API for custom integrations Auto-pulls local permit and property data Cons Pricing isn’t publicly available Some users find the learning curve steep Some users find the mobile app clunky at times ServiceTitan is management software for plumbers who’ve outgrown simpler field service tools. It can handle residential and commercial plumbing work. You can also use it to manage longer construction projects. For residential jobs, dispatchers can match plumbers to calls based on their skills and location. Once dispatched, plumbers can see the customer’s service history.. As the job wraps up, they can send invoices and collect payments from the field. The office gets those updates at the same time. ServiceTitan can also manage commercial and construction work. You can track project costs, profitability, and work in progress. It also covers inventory, service agreements, and reporting. On the marketing side, you can run campaigns and see which ads are bringing in revenue. But ServiceTitan can be harder to learn because there’s so much packed into the platform. The company doesn’t publish its pricing online, either. If you run a smaller plumbing shop and mainly need scheduling, dispatching, and invoicing, you may end up paying for features you rarely use. Hear it from a real customer: “ServiceTitan can definitely be powerful, but it’s not always plug-and-play. Setup can take time, and there’s a learning curve to really getting it dialed in the way your business needs it to run. It can also get expensive quickly…” — G2 Key features of ServiceTitan Price book management Service agreement management Inventory management Online booking Customer financing ServiceTitan pricing ServiceTitan doesn’t list pricing publicly. If you want a dedicated quote, you’ll need to reach out to their sales team. But ServiceTitan does list a few features from its three plans: Starter: Dispatching, scheduling, call booking, invoicing, and a pricebook Essentials: Mobile estimates and payroll management The Works: Configurable payroll, advanced reporting, commission tracking, and customizable memberships How to pick the right plumbing management software for you Before you buy any software, here’s a quick checklist of questions you can research and ask providers to help you get started. Pricing and contracts Is pricing per user or a flat monthly rate? How does the pricing change as your team grows? Will you need to upgrade your plan or pay extra as you add more office staff or field technicians? Are there features locked behind higher tiers that you’d realistically need to manage jobs efficiently? Is there a free demo or free trial to test the software first? Can you cancel month-to-month, or is there a minimum contract obligation? Setup and onboarding How long does the setup take for a team your size? Can you import customer records, equipment history, job notes, and service history into the platform? Can you import existing parts lists and flat-rate pricing books? What training is available to help your office team learn the system? Day-to-day usability Is the system easy to use for both office staff and plumbers? Can technicians use the mobile app while they’re on-site? Does the app work offline in basements or low-signal areas? Integrations Does it connect directly to your accounting software and payment processor? Can it integrate with the other plumbing business software you already use? Support What customer support channels can you use after you sign up? What are the support hours? Can you reach a live person if something goes wrong during evenings, weekends, or emergency calls? What features should you look for in plumbing field service software? Finding the right plumbing field service software can be difficult when so many tools offer similar features. Focus on the features below to narrow down your options and find the right fit for your team. Real-time field-to-office sync. Your office shouldn’t have to call a plumber mid-job just to get an update. Look for software that keeps job notes, photos, parts used, and job status synced between the field and office. Integration with your business phone system. A lot of plumbing work starts with a phone call. Once your field service software connects to your small business phone system, a customer’s calls, texts, and job history all show up together. Mobile app with offline access. Plumbers won’t always be in spots with good signal. Your app should keep working offline, then sync everything once you’re back in range. Smart scheduling and dispatching. When several jobs come in at once, dispatchers need to know who’s free, nearby, and qualified. Look for tools that make it easy to assign work and adjust the schedule when an emergency comes in. CRM and service history. A plumber shouldn’t show up to a repeat job without knowing what happened last time. A CRM that shows previous jobs, work completed, and customer notes in one place helps them know what they’re walking into. Quoting and invoicing or accounting integrations. Plumbing jobs may involve giving customers good-better-best options for a repair or replacement. Look for software that supports flat-rate estimates and lets customers approve them on-site. It should also turn approved estimates into invoices and sync them with accounting tools like QuickBooks. Inventory management. Parts can be spread across several trucks and your warehouse. Look for software that tracks where each item is and updates inventory as technicians use parts on jobs. Reporting and job costing. Track labor and material costs against what you charged. This shows you which jobs are profitable and helps you price similar work in the future. Where plumbing software stops, Quo picks up Good field service management software keeps plumbing jobs organized once they come in. It helps your team manage scheduling, dispatching, customer records, and payments in one place. But even the best service software won’t help if customers can’t reach you in the first place. Plumbing jobs are won or lost when someone has an emergency or is comparing you with the next business on Google. So make sure your phone system can keep up. It should keep calls, voicemails, and texts in one place with a shared inbox so any dispatcher can pick up the conversation. It should also connect with the contractor apps your team already uses, so they have the context they need before a plumber arrives on site. And when nobody is available to answer, plumbing AI can handle the call and collect the details your team needs to follow up. For a closer look at your options, see our guide to the best phone systems for plumbers . Or try Quo for free for seven days to see how it works alongside the software you already use. FAQs What software do plumbing contractors use? Depending on their needs and size, plumbing contractors typically use platforms like Jobber, Housecall Pro, and ServiceTitan. These tools handle scheduling, dispatching, and live technician tracking. Many contractors also use business phone systems like Quo for customer calls and texts. Plus, they use accounting software like QuickBooks to manage invoices, payments, and bookkeeping. How much does field service management software cost? Plumbing field service software costs vary depending on whether you’re a solo plumber or running a team. Individual plans from providers like Jobber and Housecall Pro start at around $29-$59 per month. Team plans cost more, typically ranging from about $150 to $300 per month or more, depending on the number of users and which features you need. How does plumbing service software help to grow your business? The benefits of plumbing business software include faster scheduling and better client relationships. It dispatches plumbers efficiently, sends automatic reminders, and lets you collect payment on-site. That saves time, improves cash flow, and frees up your team to take on more work.

title: Motion Detection: Why It Breaks at Enterprise Scale
summary: Motion detection can't distinguish threats from noise at enterprise scale. See why behavioral intelligence is the foundation security teams need.
body_text: Motion detection cameras break down at enterprise scale because they answer a narrow question while security teams face a much harder one: which activity matters? As camera deployments expand, simple movement alerts create more information than operators can assess with consistent speed and context. Understanding why this happens, and what can replace it, starts with what the technology was originally designed to do. The Original Purpose Behind Motion Detection Technology Motion detection is the technique enterprise security cameras and recorders use to flag frame-to-frame pixel changes as activity without identifying what caused the change. Motion-triggered recording reduced storage demands by capturing periods with activity rather than continuous footage. Operators also used those flags to decide which feeds to look at, though the technology was never built to judge what it flagged. The design question was always “Is something moving?”, never “What is happening, who is doing it, and should I care?” The system could detect that something had happened, but human operators still reviewed flagged footage to determine whether it represented a genuine threat. For facilities running small camera deployments with dedicated monitoring staff, that limitation stayed manageable. Operators applied judgment to each alert and served as the filter between pixel-change detection and genuine threat assessment. Why Everything Triggers the Same Response The technical architecture of pixel-change detection creates a fundamental problem: its output does not distinguish what caused the movement. The system registers visual changes between frames, but those changes carry no object identity, trajectory, or scene meaning. A delivery driver entering through the loading dock during business hours creates pixel changes. An unauthorized individual attempting the same entry overnight creates algorithmically identical pixel changes. Traditional systems generate the same alert for both because they process visual intensity shifts, not authorized access patterns or temporal appropriateness. Environmental factors compound the problem. Tree shadows darken and brighten pixels as they cross the frame. Headlights sweeping a parking area create dramatic intensity shifts. Rain produces widespread pixel changes, and reflections on wet pavement mimic foreground objects. Each event can generate an alert that enters the same queue as activity requiring security review. How Motion Detection Cameras Miss Real Activity False alarms get the attention, but motion detection cameras fail in the opposite direction too. Frame differencing can lose an object when it stops moving, so a person who crosses a perimeter and stands still may disappear from the algorithm’s view. Slow, steady movement toward a camera can produce frame-to-frame differences too subtle to cross the detection threshold. Fog and low light can compress the contrast the comparison depends on, and crowded scenes make it harder to isolate one person’s movement from surrounding activity. Sensitivity tuning cannot eliminate this tradeoff. Lower the threshold and environmental noise floods the alert queue; raise it and slow or distant activity may pass undetected. The Manual Verification Burden Every alert a pixel-change system generates demands the same manual verification sequence: an operator pauses other responsibilities, pulls up recorded footage or the live feed, determines whether the flagged activity is a genuine concern, and either dismisses or escalates. At enterprise scale, alarm volume can overwhelm operators and make timely review harder to sustain. The cognitive cost runs deeper than the hours. After roughly twenty minutes of watching a single screen, an operator may miss as much as 90% of what unfolds in view. When operators dismiss alert after alert that turns out to be a shadow or a headlight sweep, alert fatigue sets in: vigilance declines because experience teaches that alerts rarely indicate genuine threats. That decline reflects the volume of noise the technology produces, not operator skill or dedication. Understanding Behavioral Patterns Makes All the Difference Effective security requires knowing not just that movement occurred but what the movement means. A person sprinting across a lobby during business hours might be late to a meeting or responding to a medical emergency. The same sprint overnight demands a different response priority, a distinction pixel-change algorithms cannot make. Context spans several dimensions that motion detection technology cannot process: Temporal patterns : time of day, day of week, and seasonal rhythms define what counts as normal for each camera view. Spatial awareness : lingering near a secure server room warrants different assessment than standing in a lobby waiting area. Behavioral analysis : pacing, repeated approach-and-retreat near restricted areas, or unusual dwell times can indicate reconnaissance preceding a more serious incident. Crowding that may lead to an altercation, a person falling, or a brandished firearm are all events a pixel-change alert cannot distinguish from a passing shadow. That third category carries the highest stakes. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) describes a pathway to violence that moves through grievance, planning, preparation, and probing before an attack. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) lists observable indicators such as prolonged interest in facilities, testing or probing of security, and attempted intrusion into restricted areas. These behaviors play out on camera. A contractor photographing a data center’s cooling infrastructure during a scheduled audit is routine; the same photography from outside the perimeter fence at dusk matches the surveillance indicators organizations are advised to watch for. Pixel-change detection registers both as identical movement, or misses them entirely if the person stands still. What separates a routine delivery from a trespass is timing, dwell, and approach pattern, none of which pixel-change detection can process. How Computer Vision Improves Threat Assessment Computer vision refers to AI that identifies what appears in video, including people, vehicles, objects, and actions, rather than measuring raw pixel intensity. Reasoning Vision-Language Models (VLMs) build on that perception layer by combining visual detection with language understanding, which lets the technology interpret scenes and behaviors instead of outputting a changed-pixel mask. The shift moves the baseline of detection from pixel intensity changes to object-based classification, with people and vehicles treated as first-class categories the system reasons about directly. Reasoning approaches can establish behavioral baselines for a given location, measure how long a person lingers, and flag deviations such as repeated approaches to a restricted area or prolonged loitering. Rather than binary “motion detected” alerts, they generate assessments of how far observed behavior deviates from normal patterns for that place and period. They can also reason across more than video. When a physical access control system (PACS) logs a badge swipe, visual verification can confirm that one authorized person entered rather than several tailgating through , an event door sensors alone cannot see. Processing may occur in the cloud, on edge appliances, or through a hybrid architecture. Cloud processing can reduce on-site infrastructure but increase bandwidth use, while edge processing can reduce latency and keep more video local. Hybrid designs divide workloads according to latency, bandwidth, data privacy, and infrastructure cost requirements. In edge and hybrid models, separate edge appliances provide the intelligence; cameras remain video inputs. Comparing Motion Detection and AI Video Analytics Motion detection and reasoning AI video analytics answer different questions. Dimension Pixel-Change Motion Detection Advanced Reasoning AI Video Analytics Core question Did pixels change between frames? Can assess what is happening and whether it matters Environmental noise Shadows, rain, and headlights all trigger alerts Can classify non-threat activity and filter it Stationary subjects Lost the moment movement stops Can maintain presence when movement stops and measure dwell time Context Business hours and overnight activity are identical Can use time, location, and behavioral baselines to shape assessment Investigation Manual footage scrubbing Can support natural language search across indexed feeds Scaling Verification workload grows with camera count Can surface validated events while all feeds stay monitored The investigation row changes daily work most visibly: an operator can type “person near the loading dock after midnight” and use natural language search to retrieve matching footage quickly instead of scrubbing long recordings. Because standards such as Open Network Video Interface Forum ( ONVIF ) Profile M define how analytics metadata flows between cameras and management systems, behavioral analytics can be layered onto installed camera infrastructure rather than requiring replacement. The Scale Problem No Amount of Headcount Can Solve Camera deployments scale faster than human attention. A camera-monitoring review explains that the effective number of feeds an operator can monitor declines as scene activity increases. There are too many feeds for any operator to absorb simultaneously, regardless of skill or dedication, so in practice the vast majority of feeds go unwatched. The gap between deployment size and operator capacity is the enterprise problem. Security operations have to work as force multipliers, where technology lets small teams monitor and protect large, complex environments. When the detection layer cannot separate routine activity from genuine threats, verification demand exceeds human capacity at any team size, and the technology foundation itself has to change. Moving From Detection to Understanding The industry’s direction is explicit. AI-driven platforms are absorbing labor-intensive work such as monitoring video feeds, ranking alarms, and managing visitor access, and that shift is expected to extend across the monitoring stack from video analysis to dispatch. For security leaders evaluating the shift, a few requirements separate real behavioral intelligence from repackaged motion detection: Pilot on your own cameras across day, night, and weekend conditions, with acceptance criteria set before the trial starts. Ask vendors for false-positive and missed-detection rates in deployments similar to yours, and which field conditions can nullify the analytics. Require integration with existing cameras, video management systems (VMS), and PACS rather than infrastructure replacement. Keep humans in the loop: the technology should filter and assess, while operators judge and respond. The Security Industry Association’s SPARC report on evaluating AI vendors includes a questionnaire covering technology, data practices, and compliance that maps directly onto these questions. Motion detection did the job it was built for; protecting a modern enterprise takes behavioral intelligence. AI-Native Video Management at Enterprise Scale Trusted by Fortune 100 enterprises, Ambient.ai applies this shift through an AI-native platform where video management is built in and a reasoning Vision-Language Model (VLM) provides continuous contextual understanding across every connected feed. The approach supports a progression toward Agentic Physical Security , where AI handles continuous observation and assessment while operators remain in the loop for oversight and critical decisions. Security leaders can request a demo to evaluate the approach on their own cameras. Frequently Asked Questions How do AI-powered video analytics handle edge cases like fog, low light, or crowded scenes where traditional motion detection fails? AI-powered analytics use adaptive image enhancement and temporal modeling to track objects across lighting changes. Object segmentation separates individual trajectories and assigns persistent identifiers, isolating suspicious behavior even when multiple people move simultaneously through crowded scenes. What infrastructure changes are required to implement reasoning Vision-Language Models on an existing enterprise camera network? Reasoning VLMs integrate with existing ONVIF-compliant cameras without hardware replacement. Processing occurs on separate edge appliances that connect to current infrastructure, so organizations preserve camera investments while adding behavioral intelligence through a software and edge computing layer. How can security teams measure the reduction in false positives and missed detections when transitioning from motion detection to AI-based behavioral analytics? Establish baseline metrics tracking alert volume, operator verification time, and missed events from current motion detection systems. Run controlled pilots comparing both systems on identical camera feeds, measuring precision, recall rates, and investigation time-to-insight improvements.

title: POSCO DX Makes Major Transformation into an ‘AI Native Company’… Leading the AI Market with Physical AI and Agentic AI
summary: Posco Newsroom
body_text: POSCO DX Makes Major Transformation into an ‘AI Native Company’… Leading the AI Market with Physical AI and Agentic AI 2026/08/04 Mail facebook twitter linkedin Implementing Physical AI for Industrial Sites through Equipment Robotization and Expansion of Industrial Robots Developing a Platform to Manage the AI Agent Lifecycle and Promoting Autonomy in Office Environments The Only Full-Stack Company in Korea with Integrated Capabilities Across AI, OT, and IT Layers POSCO DX (CEO Shim Min-suk) is accelerating technology development and commercialization after declaring its transition into an “AI Native Company.” On July 29, POSCO DX held a press conference at Lotte Hotel Seoul and announced a business strategy to leap forward as an “AI Native Company,” centering on two pillars: “Physical AI” for industrial sites and “Agentic AI” for office work. First, the company is focusing on expanding Physical AI to realize an intelligent factory where the three key entities-humans, AI, and on-site equipment & robots-collaborate organically. The core idea is to achieve the robotization of equipment by integrating Physical AI technology into industrial sites to optimally control large-scale machinery. Through this, Physical AI is being applied to steel mill equipment weighing tens of tons, such as large cranes transporting steel materials, reclaimers transferring raw materials in the yard, and ship raw material unloaders, thereby ensuring worker safety and enhancing productivity. Furthermore, the company explained that it is establishing a system in which the tacit knowledge possessed by highly skilled operators is converted into core data for Physical AI, enabling AI to collaborate with humans in the on-site control room to operate robots and equipment. POSCO DX is also actively promoting the application of industrial robots in high-intensity and high-risk sites. It provides robot automation services ranging from consulting and design to construction and operation, and possesses a strength in supporting optimal robot operation by securing a platform for heterogeneous robot management in collaboration with POSCO. In particular, it designs optimal robot systems based on simulation and is pursuing the advancement of robot locomotion and manipulation through the development of VLA (Vision Language Action) models applied to mobile robots, such as humanoids. On this day, the company introduced examples of robots performing high-intensity and high-risk tasks, such as robots for removing impurities from the melting furnace in the galvanizing process of the steel mill, band cutter robots in the cold rolling process, and AGVs for automatically transporting 65-ton steel products. In addition, they shared the robotization of raw material sampling and logistics automation tasks for eco-friendly material and vehicle parts production plants. POSCO DX has independently developed ‘Agentee,’ a platform designed to implement agentic AI for office and management environments. It integrates the lifecycle of AI agents—from recruitment and evaluation to training, promotion, and retirement—much like human employees. Based on this, the company plans to promote the autonomization of office and management tasks through domain-specific ‘AI employees.’ First, AX Consulting is conducted to analyze corporate workflows and design business processes where roles are divided and performed by humans and AI agents. Based on this, Agentee develops customized agents or repurposes existing ones. A key advantage is that the entire process, from design to development, is carried out within Agentee according to standardized methodologies, enabling the rapid deployment of AI agents. At the event, examples of utilizing AI agents in tasks such as finance, human resources, labor relations, and business management were presented. It was explained that an innovative case was observed regarding the monthly recurring “pre-settlement risk check” task, where the agent automatically scanned all account categories to identify abnormal accounts and missing vouchers, and even generated risk reports, thereby reducing the task time from approximately three hours to within one minute. The company expects that expanding the application of AI agents to the entire accounting settlement process will improve productivity by at least 30% compared to the current level. Currently, the company has developed and is operating over 200 AI agents for POSCO Group companies, including POSCO DX, and plans to establish and disseminate a standard model for the group while supplying the verified platform to the external market. A POSCO DX official emphasized, “As the only full-stack company in Korea equipped with integrated capabilities across all levels from operational systems (OT) to IT, we will leap forward as the company that best implements physical AI and agentic AI services by integrating AX technology based on our combined capabilities and understanding of physical and office domains.” Meanwhile, POSCO Group has established a ‘Mission-oriented AX’ strategy and is accelerating its major AI transformation centered on three axes: Process, Work, and Value. Furthermore, at the CEO Investor Day held on July 2, the group unveiled a vision to establish a ‘Triple-core’ system encompassing industrial resources (steel), strategic resources (lithium, cathode and anode materials, rare earth elements, etc.), and energy resources (LNG, renewable energy). In addition, regarding new business areas, the group announced plans to commercialize physical AI for the process industry, based on the experience in equipment automation and intelligence accumulated in the steel sector and a vast amount of field data. ▲ ▲ POSCO DX’s Sim-to-Real Simulation for Robot Automation of the Drive Motor Core Stator Production Line at POSCO Mobility Solution ▲ POSCO DX’s Sim-to-Real Simulation for Robot Automation of the Drive Motor Core Stator Production Line at POSCO Mobility Solution Agentic AI AI AI Native Company physical AI POSCO DX

title: Charles Schwab IMPACT 2026: Attendee travel guide
summary: : Plan your trip to Charles Schwab IMPACT 2026 with tips for Boston hotels, BOS transportation, conference costs, The Exchange, and your agenda.
body_text: IMPACT 2026, hosted by Charles Schwab, will bring registered investment advisers and other wealth management professionals to Boston for three days of education, networking, The Exchange, and conversations about firm growth, technology, and practice management.[1][2][3] With an agenda spanning education sessions, keynotes, Territory Dinners, and networking events, planning your hotel, transportation, and schedule ahead of time can help you get more from the conference and bring useful ideas and connections back to your firm. What is IMPACT 2026 and who is it for? IMPACT is Charles Schwab's premier gathering for registered investment advisers, with programming focused on education, industry connections, and ideas for growing and managing an independent firm.[1] IMPACT 2026 takes place Oct. 27–29 at the Thomas M. Menino Convention & Exhibition Center in Boston, with the Final Night Event at MGM Music Hall at Fenway.[1][3][4] The invitation-only conference brings together independent advisers, RIA firm leaders and teams, Schwab representatives, industry experts, and companies serving the wealth management industry.[1][2][3] Programming includes keynotes, education sessions, The Exchange, Territory Dinners, and networking events throughout the three-day conference.[4] Before the conference, identify the topics and challenges most relevant to your firm. Use those priorities to choose education sessions, decide which companies to visit in The Exchange, and make time to connect with peers facing similar business and practice management challenges. What makes IMPACT 2026 worth the trip IMPACT brings together Schwab leaders, industry experts, other registered investment advisers, and companies serving the wealth management industry. Education sessions offer opportunities to explore topics related to firm growth, technology, practice management, and other challenges facing RIAs, while The Exchange and networking events give attendees time to connect with peers and industry providers.[1][4] Plan around these in-person experiences: Education sessions and keynotes: Hear from Schwab leaders and industry experts on topics relevant to managing and growing an independent advisory firm.[1][4] The Exchange: Meet companies serving the wealth management industry, explore technology and services, and connect with exhibitors throughout the conference.[4] Territory Dinners: Connect with other attendees outside the main conference programming during Tuesday evening's Territory Dinners.[4] Welcome Reception and Cocktails & Connections: Make time for additional opportunities to meet peers, Schwab representatives, and industry partners during the conference.[4] Final Night Event: Close out IMPACT at MGM Music Hall at Fenway, where Zac Brown Band will perform Thursday evening.[1][4] What you learn at IMPACT can help inform priorities back at your firm. Focus your schedule on sessions, conversations, and companies that relate to the challenges you're working on now, whether that means evaluating technology, improving firm operations, exploring growth strategies, or learning how other advisers are approaching similar issues. Where to stay for IMPACT 2026 Schwab's official IMPACT hotel block includes several properties within a half-mile of the Thomas M. Menino Convention & Exhibition Center, along with additional options near Boston Common, Back Bay, and downtown Boston.[15] Staying in the Seaport gives you the shortest trip to conference programming, while the farther official hotels may offer different rates, amenities, or access to other parts of Boston. Hotels by distance to the convention center Compare the official IMPACT hotel options by distance and conference rates, which are available Oct. 27–29:[15] Area Distance to venue Details IMPACT rates Seaport 0.1–0.5 mile There are nine official hotels within a half-mile of the convention center, including the Omni Boston Hotel at the Seaport, The Westin Boston Seaport District, Seaport Hotel Boston, and Hyatt Place Boston/Seaport District. $329–$399 per night plus taxes Boston Common / Back Bay 1.5–1.6 miles Revere Hotel Boston Common and Hilton Boston Park Plaza are part of the official IMPACT block but require a longer trip to the convention center. $326–$349 per night plus taxes Downtown Boston 1.1 miles Hyatt Regency Boston is part of the official IMPACT block and requires a longer trip to the convention center than the Seaport properties. $369 per night plus taxes For the shortest trip to sessions and The Exchange, start with the official Seaport properties closest to the convention center. If those hotels are unavailable or don't fit your budget, compare the other properties in Schwab's block with additional Boston hotels based on price and transportation. Official IMPACT rates are available through Sept. 24, 2026, or until the room block sells out.[15] Boston hotel pricing for IMPACT 2026 Navan looked at anonymized hotel booking patterns during IMPACT 2025 in Boston to provide context for hotel pricing.[7] Use these benchmarks while planning your 2026 trip: Median hotel rate: During conference week, the median nightly rate near the event venue was $623.[7] Stay length: Business travelers stayed an average of 2.1 nights.[7] Late bookings: Roughly 49% of bookings were made within two weeks of arrival.[7] Schwab offers negotiated rates at official IMPACT hotels across Boston, including several properties within a half-mile of the convention center.[15] If the official IMPACT block is sold out or the available rates don't fit your travel policy, compare other hotels in the Seaport and downtown Boston. Staying outside the block can give you more choices, but check the distance to the convention center and your transportation options before booking. Boston flight trends Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) is the primary airport for IMPACT attendees, about 3.5 miles from the convention center.[5][8] Navan flight data from IMPACT week 2025 shows 796 business flights into Boston, with 9.0% arriving from international origins.[7] The most common origin cities were New York, Chicago, Washington, D.C., Atlanta, and Newark.[7] Schwab recommends arriving Monday, Oct. 26, or early Tuesday, Oct. 27, and departing late Thursday, Oct. 29, or Friday, Oct. 30.[3] A Monday arrival gives you additional time to settle in before Tuesday afternoon programming, which includes education sessions, The Exchange, the opening keynote, Welcome Reception, and Territory Dinners. How Navan Edge helps you book your conference travel Use Navan Edge, your travel assistant powered by AI and with human travel experts available 24/7, to plan and book your IMPACT 2026 trip. Compare flights, hotels, and restaurants using live availability, personal preferences, and all the amenities that are important to you , then book everything in the same thread without juggling multiple apps or websites. Continue earning your usual airline miles and hotel loyalty points, get your credit card points, and earn an additional 5% back in Amazon Gift Cards on eligible hotel stays. See our travel rewards on business trips guide for a closer look at how it works. How to budget for conference travel to Boston A trip to IMPACT includes more than your conference registration. Budget for Boston lodging, transportation to and from BOS, local transit or rideshare, meals outside conference programming, and other incidentals before you travel. Federal per diem for Boston The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) sets federal per diem rates by location and fiscal year. IMPACT 2026 takes place in October 2026, which falls in FY2027. At the time of publication, GSA had not yet published FY2027 rates, so the FY2026 rates below can provide a benchmark for planning but will not be the applicable rates for the conference. For October 2025, the FY2026 rates for Boston and Cambridge were: $441 per day combined: Includes $349 for nightly lodging plus $92 for daily meals and incidental expenses (M&IE)[6] M&IE breakdown: Includes $23 for breakfast, $26 for lunch, $38 for dinner, and $5 for incidentals (reduce your meal allowance for any catering at the event)[6] First and last travel days: Includes an M&IE allowance of $69 (i.e., 75% of the daily M&IE rate)[6] For context, Schwab's official IMPACT 2026 hotel rates range from $326–$399 per night plus taxes, putting several options close to the FY2026 October lodging benchmark of $349.[6][15] FY2027 rates may differ, so check the updated GSA rate before you travel, and use your company's travel and expense policy to determine the limits that apply to your trip. Other expenses to consider Planning for these expenses before you book can help you estimate the full cost of your IMPACT trip and avoid surprises while traveling. Conference registration: Standard registration costs $1,995 from Aug. 27 through Oct. 26, with onsite registration increasing to $2,300 beginning Oct. 27. Check the IMPACT website for current pricing before you register.[2] Group registration: Firms registering four or more attendees can save $100 per person when eligible registrations are completed by Sept. 18.[2] Conference meals: Registration includes conference receptions, breakfasts, lunches, and breaks on main conference days, so adjust your M&IE reimbursement accordingly.[3] Airport transfer: The Silver Line SL1 is free from BOS into Boston, while MBTA fares for the return trip and rideshare costs should be included in your transportation budget.[5][8][9] Client and team dinners: Budget separately for restaurant meals, particularly if you're planning dinners outside official IMPACT programming. Additional transportation: Include local transit or rideshare costs for trips between your hotel, the convention center, dinners, and the Final Night Event at MGM Music Hall at Fenway. Plan your IMPACT agenda IMPACT combines keynotes and education sessions with The Exchange, Territory Dinners, and other networking events throughout the three-day conference.[4] Start with the sessions most relevant to your firm, then leave room for The Exchange and conversations with other attendees and industry providers. Schwab plans to make the full session catalog available through the IMPACT event hub in late September, when attendees can use Schedule Builder to create a personal agenda.[1][4] Until then, use the published agenda to plan around the conference's major events: Tuesday (Oct. 27): Education sessions begin at 2 p.m., followed by The Exchange, the opening keynote, Welcome Reception, and Territory Dinners[4] Wednesday (Oct. 28): Breakfast in The Exchange, a morning keynote, education sessions, Lunch & Learn, an afternoon keynote, and Cocktails & Connections[4] Thursday (Oct. 29): Breakfast in The Exchange, education sessions, Lunch & Learn, an afternoon keynote, and the Final Night Event from 7–10 p.m. at MGM Music Hall at Fenway[4] Conference programming begins Tuesday at 2 p.m. and concludes with the Final Night Event Thursday at 10 p.m.[2][3][4] Build flexibility into your schedule Once Schedule Builder opens, add your highest-priority education sessions first. Schwab recommends registering for sessions in advance, but leave some openings in your agenda for The Exchange, networking events, and conversations that come up during the conference.[1][4] Keep these priorities in mind as you build your schedule: Education sessions: Prioritize topics that align with the challenges and opportunities most relevant to your firm, and register for your preferred sessions in advance.[1][4] The Exchange: Set aside time to meet exhibitors, explore technology and services, and connect with companies serving the wealth management industry.[4] Keynotes: Plan around the main-stage programming before filling the rest of your agenda with education sessions and meetings.[4] Logistics: Check event locations and travel time, particularly for Thursday's Final Night Event at MGM Music Hall at Fenway.[3][4] Our business trip planning guide covers general flight, hotel, and other travel planning beyond this IMPACT-specific checklist. What to pack and wear at IMPACT Business casual is a practical choice for most of IMPACT, with comfortable, polished clothing that works for education sessions, The Exchange, and networking events. Pack comfortable shoes for long days at the convention center, along with a slightly dressier option if you have business dinners or meetings planned. Boston is typically cool in late October, with daytime highs in the upper 50s°F and overnight lows in the mid-40s°F.[10] Rain is also possible, and the Seaport can feel colder and windier along the waterfront. Pack layers that work indoors and outside, plus a warmer jacket for evenings and Thursday's Final Night Event at MGM Music Hall at Fenway. Conference essentials Boston's late-October weather, waterfront location, and long conference days make layers and comfortable footwear especially useful. Add these essentials to your packing list: Two pairs of comfortable shoes: Alternate pairs during the conference to give your feet a break after long days at the convention center and walking around Boston. Portable charger: Using the IMPACT event hub, maps, messaging, and other apps throughout the day can drain your battery. Reusable water bottle: Keep water with you during long stretches of keynotes, education sessions, and time in The Exchange. Sweater or blazer: Bring an extra layer for conference rooms and changing temperatures throughout the day. Warm, weather-resistant jacket: Late-October temperatures can feel colder around the Seaport, particularly when it's windy or after dark. Compact umbrella: Boston can be rainy in October, so keep one in your conference bag for walks between your hotel and the venue. Snacks: Keep a protein bar or another easy snack in your bag in case conference programming overlaps with your usual meal times. Hand sanitizer and cough drops: It's the start of cold and flu season, so keep both in your day bag for long days in crowded conference spaces. Getting from the airport to IMPACT 2026 Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) is about 3.5 miles from the Thomas M. Menino Convention & Exhibition Center, making the airport relatively close to the IMPACT venue.[5][8] Schwab recommends arriving Monday, Oct. 26, or early Tuesday, Oct. 27, before conference programming begins at 2 p.m. Tuesday.[3] If you're staying in the Seaport, public transit, rideshare, and taxis all provide options for getting from BOS to your hotel or the convention center. Option Time Cost Notes MBTA Silver Line SL1 20–30 minutes Free from BOS into Boston Serves all airport terminals and stops at World Trade Center, a short walk from the convention center[5][8][9] Rideshare 10–20 minutes Varies Uber and Lyft are available at BOS; fares and travel times vary with traffic and demand[8][9] Taxi 10–20 minutes Varies Taxis are available at Logan and offer direct transportation to Seaport hotels and the convention center[8][9] For travelers staying in the Seaport, the Silver Line SL1 offers a direct public transit option from BOS without requiring a transfer. Rideshare or taxi may be more convenient if you have substantial luggage, arrive late, or are staying farther from the Silver Line. Beyond sessions: Make time for The Exchange and evening networking Some of the most useful conversations at IMPACT can happen outside scheduled education sessions and keynotes. Leave time in your agenda for The Exchange, Territory Dinners, networking events, and conversations with other advisers and industry providers rather than filling every hour with scheduled programming. Identify exhibitors before you arrive: Review The Exchange exhibitors in advance and make a short list of companies you want to visit based on your firm's current priorities. Make time for The Exchange: Set aside dedicated time to explore technology and services, speak with exhibitors, and follow up on questions from education sessions rather than squeezing visits between other activities. Plan around networking events: The Welcome Reception, Territory Dinners, and Cocktails & Connections provide additional opportunities to connect with other attendees outside education sessions and keynotes. Take notes after conversations: Jot down useful ideas, resources, and next steps while the details are still fresh. Follow up within 48 hours: Send a short email or LinkedIn message with a clear next step, whether that's sharing a resource, continuing a conversation, or making an introduction. Build in short breaks: Long conference days can be tiring. Leave enough space in your schedule to grab water, have a snack, or take a short walk along the Seaport before your next activity. Focus on conversations that relate to your firm's priorities and make a note of any follow-up before moving on to your next session or meeting. A few useful conversations you continue after IMPACT can be more valuable than trying to meet as many people as possible. What to eat at IMPACT 2026 Start conference days with a filling breakfast, especially when your agenda includes morning programming followed by education sessions and time in The Exchange. Keep a protein bar or another easy snack in your bag in case sessions or meetings overlap with your usual meal times. These Boston restaurants offer several options beyond the conference venue: Seaport seafood: Row 34 serves New England seafood and has private-event options for group dinners in Fort Point.[11] Back Bay steakhouse: Abe & Louie's serves classic steakhouse fare for lunch and dinner and offers private and semi-private group dining.[12] Group dining: Yvonne's offers globally inspired shareable dishes in Downtown Boston, with several spaces available for group and private dining.[13] Upscale steakhouse: Mooo.... Beacon Hill serves steak and seafood and offers private dining for business meals and groups.[14] For business dinners and group meals, consider making reservations before you arrive, particularly if you need a specific time or space for a larger group. Navan Edge can also help you find and reserve Boston restaurants in the same chat where you booked your flight and hotel. Finish strong on departure day A little preparation before departure can make your final IMPACT day easier, particularly if you're checking out before Thursday's programming and Final Night Event are over. Pack before checkout: Set aside your travel clothes, charge your devices, and check the room for chargers, adapters, and other easy-to-miss items. Ask about late checkout: If you have a late Thursday or Friday flight, check with your hotel about late checkout or luggage storage so you don't have to carry your bags through conference programming. Allow enough time at BOS: Plan to arrive at least two hours before a domestic flight and three hours before an international flight, with additional time for travel from your hotel or the Seaport to the airport. File expenses promptly: Upload receipts and note any expenses that require additional documentation while the details are still fresh. Use airport downtime: If you have lounge access or time before boarding, use it to organize notes, receipts, and follow-up tasks. Plan your follow-up: Set aside time after IMPACT to share useful takeaways with your team and reconnect with people you met during the conference. Make the most of your IMPACT 2026 trip Plan your hotel, transportation, and budget before you arrive, then build your agenda around the sessions and experiences most relevant to your firm. Leave time for The Exchange, Territory Dinners, and conversations with other attendees, and follow up on useful connections and ideas after the conference. A little planning can help you spend less time managing trip logistics and more time getting value from your time in Boston. Planning your IMPACT 2026 trip? body_text: CoStar Expects U.S. Industrial Demand to Outpace Supply by Late 2027 August 5, 2026 PDF Version ARLINGTON, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 5, 2026-- U.S. industrial vacancy is expected to rise slightly through early 2027 before making a gradual descent, according to a revised forecast from CoStar , the leading global provider of online real estate marketplaces, information and analytics in the property markets. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260805646623/en/ Industrial deliveries to outpace demand into 2027 The national industrial vacancy rate remains in the mid-7% range entering the third quarter of 2026 and is expected to edge higher into 2027 before beginning a steady decline. This is a modest improvement from the previous forecast , as stronger-than-expected demand in recent quarters has led to an upward revision in near-term net absorption and a slightly lower vacancy outlook. Average annual rent growth over the 2026-27 period has also been revised higher and is now forecasted at +1.9%. “While leasing activity remains healthy, elevated availability and a lingering supply overhang are expected to keep rent growth modest in the near term,” said Juan Arias, national director of industrial analytics at CoStar Group. “By late 2027, slowing construction activity and improving demand should allow net absorption to exceed new supply, marking a turning point for market fundamentals.” “Risks to the forecast remain tilted to the downside,” said Arias. “Trade and tariff uncertainty, elevated operating costs, and subdued consumer spending on goods could weigh on tenant expansion plans and delay the recovery in demand. Under a weaker economic scenario, vacancy could rise above the current forecast and place additional pressure on rents. Conversely, easing inflation, stronger consumer confidence, and continued resilience in leasing activity could support faster absorption and an earlier recovery.” The full forecast can be found here . title: How Bengaluru Brain Power Is Helping Advance the Future of Flight
summary: In his 26 years at GE Aerospace, Consulting Engineer Nitesh Jain has learned to expect great things from his colleagues at Bengaluru’s
body_text: In his 26 years at GE Aerospace, Consulting Engineer Nitesh Jain has learned to expect great things from his colleagues at Bengaluru’s John F. Welch Technology Centre (JFWTC). One of the company’s largest multidisciplinary centers for research and development outside the United States, the JFWTC has long collaborated with other global research centers to produce key innovations for the future of flight. Now, with the company riding a wave of media attention for the advances in high-altitude hybrid electric flight technology announced at the recent Farnborough International Airshow , Jain points to a step change that’s significant even for the Future of Flight teams in Bengaluru. “In the past, we’ve worked on several engine lines — GE90 , GEnx , GE9X , CFM LEAP * — and with each change of the center line, we’ve brought an additional 10% to 15% fuel benefit,” Jain says. “This time, we’re looking to double that.” Using next-generation propulsion technologies like Open Fan architecture, compact core, and hybrid electric systems, engineers of the CFM RISE* program have targeted a 20% leap in fuel efficiency over current engines while still meeting durability expectations, and they are drawing on the Bengaluru technology center’s combined expertise in a range of advanced aerospace technologies. “We found the only way to get this kind of step change in fuel-burn efficiency without excessive weight and drag is to remove the constraints of the engine’s cover,” Jain explains. The ductless Open Fan design in the RISE program allows for a larger fan diameter, which in turn pushes more air around the compressor, producing more thrust. Internally, compact-core technology enhances capabilities inside the high-pressure compressor and high-pressure turbine. The combination of the unique fan blade system, aerodynamic design, advanced compact core, and adaptive cycle engine capability, which optimizes engine performance at every stage of flight, aims to boost durability and reduce dust ingestion in hot and harsh environments. Pushing the envelope in this kind of space requires expertise in areas beyond conventional engine technologies. “It’s a combination of aerodynamics, thermal systems design, structures design, systems analysis, advanced materials, and additive manufacturing,” says Jain. “All these and more play a role in addressing future aviation demands — in weight, fuel burn, efficiency, operability, durability, and manufacturability.” Demands that the engineering teams in Bengaluru are uniquely suited to meet. Bending Physics to Speed Innovation Take aeroacoustics, a field of particular importance to Open Fan technology. Since this architecture omits a noise-reducing nacelle, engineers needed to design quieter blades, which meant understanding noise sources. Ravish Karve, an advanced lead engineer at Bengaluru’s research center, pursued this collaboratively with GE Aerospace teams worldwide. Together they leveraged one of the world’s largest supercomputers — Frontier, based at the U.S. Department of Energy’s Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee — to run computational fluid dynamics software that simulated the air movement and acoustics of a full-scale Open Fan design. Frontier has the processing power of roughly 37,000 GPUs and can make more than a quintillion calculations per second. “We found that we could bend some of the physics rules favorably for this particular application,” says Karve, who focused on the static outlet guide vanes (OGV) behind the front fan that guide air, which is subject to the intense distortion in a noise-producing wake. Research revealed that the optimal arrangement of these OGVs is a counterintuitively uneven placement around the engine — the kind of breakthrough that Karve anticipates seeing more often from Bengaluru’s research center. “We’re currently working on AI projects and collaborating across engineering, research, and data science, all co-located at the same center,” he says. “In the era of AI, multiple models must be connected to each other, and having those voices co-located speeds innovation.” From left: Nitesh Jain, Sumitha Mohan, and Ravish Karve inside GE Aerospace's research center in Bengaluru. An Interdisciplinary Effort Some of the innovations adapt known technology, as in electric vehicles, to aviation. Bengaluru’s Senior Engineer Sumitha Mohan has spent four years adapting hybrid electronics for aircraft, where the technology faces much stricter, more diverse challenges. “Cars are designed to operate at sea level, at normal temperatures, with relatively few weight demands,” says Mohan. “With aircraft, you need systems as power-dense as possible, so as not to negatively affect fuel burn, and that can operate at high ambient conditions.” Not to mention at altitudes above 30,000 feet. “You can’t buy these kinds of conversion systems off the shelf,” she adds. “You need to design them.” Mohan’s team is working on new hybrid electric systems that seek to replace traditionally pneumatic, hydraulic, or mechanical systems, and do so efficiently enough to help deliver the 20% leap in fuel efficiency that the RISE program is aiming for. The robust interdisciplinary environment at Bengaluru has been an advantage. “One major breakthrough has been integrating a megawatt-scale hybrid system into an aircraft that can operate at altitude,” Mohan says. “That’s simply not been done before: taking the entire aircraft’s electrical system and making something that’s extremely efficient and operates seamlessly with whatever is currently on board the aircraft.” This advance has required thermal engineers, mechanical system designers, and a wide variety of experts in a tremendous range of fields. “It’s a very interdisciplinary effort with a multi-team network across different sites.” ‘A Lot of Teams Working Together’ The close proximity of engineers at the JFWTC enables them to move faster from idea to analysis, validation, and learning, as do India-based collaborators that include the National Aerospace Laboratory, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), and the Indian Institute of Science. And this is just on the R&D side. “On top of this, our services engineering team is co-located at the Bengaluru center, which provides in-region support to our airline customers in South Asia and the Middle East. This helps give us a deeper understanding of reliability, fuel burn, durability, maintainability, and turnaround,” Jain adds. “It’s about understanding how to deliver practical value in services.” At the Farnborough International Airshow, GE Aerospace provided an in-depth look at the advances the company is making in high-altitude hybrid electric flight. But these breakthroughs only hint at how forward-looking the work being done in Bengaluru is, and how it contributes to technology maturation with a focus on safety, durability, and efficiency. “A lot of technologies had to come together to make that happen,” says Jain. “A lot of teams working together, a lot of expertise that’s been tested in separate pieces, coming together as an integrated system for the first time. That tells the story of just how much success is behind the technology.” * CFM LEAP engines are produced by CFM International, a 50-50 joint company between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines. RISE is a technology development program of CFM. It is not a product offered for commercial sale.

First Mid has received its fourth consecutive Top Workplaces Financial Services Industry award, along with seven Top Workplaces Culture Excellence awards recognizing its strengths in Compensation & Benefits, Employee Appreciation, Employee Well-Being, Innovation, Professional Development, Purpose & Values, and Work-Life Flexibility. Together, these awards reflect a workplace defined by trust, collaboration, and the everyday contributions of employees. “One of First Mid’s greatest strengths has always been our people," said Matt Smith, Chief Executive Officer and President at First Mid. “As we continue to grow, our focus is on ensuring First Mid remains a place where employees can expand their skills, take on new challenges, and see a future for themselves.
